globals.name: _G
globals.documentation: Type: Array A table that is shared between all scripts of the same context level. Any value written to _G from one script is visible to every other script at that same context level, which makes it a simple way to share state between scripts.

globals.name: _VERSION
globals.documentation: Type: string A global variable (not a function) that holds a string containing the current interpreter version.

globals.name: assert
globals.documentation: Throws an error if the provided value is false or nil. If the assertion passes, it returns all values passed to it. Assert Demonstrates the assert global.

globals.name: collectgarbage
globals.documentation: Performs the specified operation of the garbage collector. Note that Roblox's Luau sandbox only allows the count option to be used (the total memory in use by Luau, in kilobytes), as other options can interfere with existing processes. Effectively, this makes LuaGlobals.gcinfo() a superior alternative that should be used instead. returns the total memory in use in kilobytes.

globals.name: DebuggerManager
globals.documentation: Deprecated: The DebuggerManager is obsolete and serves little to no use case for developers. Returns the legacy DebuggerManager class which acts as an interface for Roblox's Luau debugger feature. This function is not recognized by Luau's analysis tool and will raise an undefined global warning.

globals.name: delay
globals.documentation: Deprecated: This method has been superseded by task.delay() and should not be used for future work. Schedules a function to be executed after delayTime seconds have passed, without yielding the current thread. This function allows multiple Luau threads to be executed in parallel from the same stack. The delay will have a minimum duration of 29 milliseconds, but this minimum may be higher depending on the target framerate and various throttling conditions. If the delayTime parameter is not specified, the minimum duration will be used.

globals.name: elapsedTime
globals.documentation: Returns how much time has elapsed since the current instance of Roblox was started. In Roblox Studio, this begins counting up from the moment Roblox Studio starts running, not just when opening a place. started running.

globals.name: Enum
globals.documentation: Registry of engine enum types.

globals.name: error
globals.documentation: Raise a Luau runtime error.

globals.name: game
globals.documentation: Root DataModel for the running experience.

globals.name: gcinfo
globals.documentation: Returns the total memory heap size in kilobytes. The number reflects the current heap consumption from the operating system perspective, which fluctuates over time as garbage collector frees objects.

globals.name: getfenv
globals.documentation: Deprecated: This function allows uncontrolled change of the global/function environment and disables script optimizations. Changes to the environment are not tracked by the script analysis tooling and may result in missing or incorrect warnings. As a replacement, consider using debug.info() instead. Returns the current environment in use by the caller, as a dictionary. WARNING: This function allows uncontrolled change of the global/function environment and disables script optimizations. Changes to the environment are not tracked by the script analysis tooling and may result in missing or incorrect warnings. As a replacement, consider using debug.info() instead.

globals.name: getmetatable
globals.documentation: Returns the metatable of the given value t if it has one, otherwise returns nil. If t does have a metatable, and the __metatable metamethod is set, it returns that value instead. t can be a value of any type, not only a table, and this function doesn't error when t isn't a table. However, it doesn't always return nil for non-table values. Strings and many Roblox types, such as Instance, have locked metatables, so this function returns the string "The metatable is locked" for them. To check whether a value uses a specific metatable, compare the result directly, such as getmetatable(value) == MyClass.

globals.name: Instance
globals.documentation: Factory and base class for engine instances.

globals.name: ipairs
globals.documentation: Returns three values: an iterator function, the table t and the number 0. Each time the iterator function is called, it returns the next numerical index-value pair in the table. When used in a generic for-loop, the return values can be used to iterate over each numerical index in the table: call. The table t passed as the invariant state. The initial control value 0. Ipairs Demonstrates the ipairs global.

globals.name: loadstring
globals.documentation: Loads Luau code from a string and returns it as a function. Unlike standard Lua 5.1, Roblox's Luau cannot load the compiled bytecode using loadstring(). loadstring() is disabled by default. For guidance around enabling it, see ServerScriptService. WARNING: This method disables certain Luau optimizations on the returned function. Extreme caution should be taken when using LuaGlobals.loadstring(); if your intention is to allow users to run code in your experience, make sure to protect the returned function's environment by using LuaGlobals.getfenv() and LuaGlobals.setfenv(). message string on failure.

globals.name: newproxy
globals.documentation: Creates a blank zero-size userdata with the option for it to have a metatable. If addMetatable is true, an empty metatable is created and assigned to the userdata; you can then retrieve it with LuaGlobals.getmetatable() and populate it with metamethods. If addMetatable is false or omitted, the userdata has no metatable and only serves as a unique identity token. Unlike host-created userdata (Roblox instances), a newproxy-created userdata always reports "userdata" from both LuaGlobals.type() and typeof(); setting a __type metamethod on it does not change the typeof() result. addMetatable is true.

globals.name: next
globals.signature: next(t: table, lastKey?: Variant): Variant, Variant
globals.documentation: Returns the first key/value pair in the array. If a lastKey argument was specified then returns the next element in the array based on the key that provided. The order in which the indices are enumerated is not specified, even for numeric indices. To traverse a table in numeric order, use a numerical for loop or ipairs. The behavior of next is undefined if, during the traversal, you assign any value to a non-existent field in the table. You may, however, modify existing fields. In particular, you may clear existing fields.

globals.name: pairs
globals.documentation: Returns an iterator function, the passed table t, and nil, so that the construction will iterate over all key/value pairs of that table when used in a generic for loop: Pairs Demonstrates the pairs global.

globals.name: pcall
globals.signature: pcall(func: function, args: Tuple): bool, Variant
globals.documentation: Calls the function func with the given arguments in protected mode. This means that any error inside func is not propagated; instead, pcall() catches the error and returns a status code. Its first result is the status code (a boolean), which is true if the call succeeds without errors. In such case, pcall() also returns all results from the call, after this first result. In case of any error, pcall() returns false plus the error message. failure. Pcall Demonstrates the pcall global.

globals.name: plugin
globals.documentation: Type: Plugin A reference to the Plugin object that represents the plugin being run from this Script. This reference exists only in the context where a script is executed as a plugin and is not passed to ModuleScripts within the plugin. To use this reference in a ModuleScript, you must explicitly pass it. Roblox Globals Plugin Demonstrates the plugin global.

globals.name: PluginManager
globals.documentation: Returns the PluginManager which is a deprecated singleton that was previously required to create plugins. It still has some applicable uses, such as if you need to create a Plugin object from Studio's Command Bar.

globals.name: print
globals.documentation: Write values to the Studio output.

globals.name: printidentity
globals.documentation: Prints Current identity is [ID] to the output, where [ID] corresponds to the current thread's security context level.

globals.name: rawequal
globals.documentation: Checks whether v1 is equal to v2 without invoking the __eq metamethod. The comparison uses primitive equality rules: values of different types are never equal; nil equals only itself; numbers and vectors are compared by value; booleans are compared by value; and all reference types (tables, functions, threads, userdata) are compared by identity (same object in memory). This is useful when you need to compare two tables or userdata objects that have an __eq metamethod and you want to test whether they are literally the same object rather than semantically equal. invocation, false otherwise.

globals.name: rawget
globals.documentation: Gets the real value of table[index] without invoking the __index metamethod. The first argument must be a table; the second can be any non-nil value. If the key does not exist in the table itself, rawget() returns nil rather than walking up the metatable chain. This is useful for inspecting a table's own stored fields when a metatable-based lookup chain would otherwise intercept the access. the table itself.

globals.name: rawlen
globals.documentation: Returns the length of a table or string without invoking the __len metamethod. The argument must be a table or string; passing any other type raises an argument error. For tables, the result is equivalent to what the # operator would return before any metamethod fires; the length of the array portion as determined by the boundary search. For strings, it returns the byte count.

globals.name: rawset
globals.signature: rawset(t: table, index: Variant, value: Variant): table
globals.documentation: Sets table[index] to value without invoking the __newindex metamethod. The first argument must be a table, the second is the key (must not be nil), and the third is the value to assign. Returns the table itself, which allows chained calls when building tables that have a __newindex guard. This is the complement of LuaGlobals.rawget() for write operations; use it when you need to bypass a proxy table's write interception.

globals.name: require
globals.documentation: Load a ModuleScript.

globals.name: script
globals.documentation: The Script, LocalScript, or ModuleScript currently executing.

globals.name: select
globals.documentation: Returns all arguments after argument number index. If negative, it will return from the end of the argument list. If the index argument is set to "#", the number of arguments that were passed after it is returned. index is "#". Select Demonstrates the select global.

globals.name: setfenv
globals.documentation: Deprecated: This function allows uncontrolled change of the global/function environment and disables script optimizations. Changes to the environment are not tracked by the script analysis tooling and may result in missing or incorrect warnings. Sets the environment to be used by the given function. f can be a function or a number that specifies the function at that stack level: Level 1 is the function calling setfenv(). setfenv() returns the given function. If f is 0, then setfenv() changes the environment of the running thread and returns no values. WARNING: This function allows uncontrolled change of the global/function environment and disables script optimizations. Changes to the environ

globals.name: setmetatable
globals.documentation: Sets the metatable for the given table t to newMeta. If newMeta is nil, the metatable of t is removed. Finally, this function returns the table t which was passed to it. If t already has a metatable whose __metatable metamethod is set, calling this on t raises an error. newMeta. Setmetatable Demonstrates the setmetatable global.

globals.name: settings
globals.documentation: Returns the GlobalSettings object, which can be used to access the settings objects that are used in Roblox Studio's settings menu. objects.

globals.name: shared
globals.documentation: Type: Array A table that is shared across all scripts that share the same execution context level. This serves the exact same purpose as _G.

globals.name: spawn
globals.documentation: Deprecated: This method has been superseded by task.spawn() and should not be used for future work. Runs the specified callback function in a separate thread, without yielding the current thread. The function will be executed the next time Roblox's Task Scheduler runs an update cycle. This delay will take at least 29 milliseconds but can arbitrarily take longer, depending on the target framerate and various throttling conditions. The callback function is invoked with two arguments: 1. The first being the amount of time which elapsed from when spawn was called to when the function was invoked. 2. The second being equivalent to elapsedTime() or roughly how long the engine has been running.

globals.name: stats
globals.documentation: Returns the Stats service. It is preferred that developers use ServiceProvider:GetService() to retrieve it instead.

globals.name: tick
globals.documentation: Returns how much time has elapsed, in seconds, since the Unix epoch, on the current local session's computer. The Unix epoch is represented by 00:00:00 on 1 January 1970. tick() isn't officially deprecated, but has a variety of issues. It can be off by up to one second and returns inconsistent results across time zones and operating systems. Use os.time(), os.clock(), or RobloxGlobals.time() instead. Also consider DateTime.UnixTimestamp and DateTime.UnixTimestampMillis. according to the local device clock.

globals.name: time
globals.documentation: Returns the amount of time, in seconds, that has elapsed since the current game instance started running. If the current game instance is not running, this will be 0. If Workspace.AuthorityMode is AuthorityMode.Server, this value is synchronized between client and server. running.

globals.name: tonumber
globals.documentation: Attempts to convert the arg into a number with a specified base to interpret the value in. If it cannot be converted, this function returns nil. The base may be any integer between 2 and 36, inclusive. In bases above 10, the letter 'A' (in either upper or lower case) represents 10, 'B' represents 11, and so forth, with 'Z' representing 35. In base 10 (the default), the number may have a decimal part, as well as an optional exponent part. In other bases, only unsigned integers are accepted. If a string begins with 0x and a base is not provided, the 0x is trimmed and the base is assumed to be 16, or hexadecimal.

globals.name: tostring
globals.documentation: Receives an argument of any type and converts it to a string in a reasonable format. For complete control of how numbers are converted, use string.format. If the metatable of e has a __tostring metamethod, then it will be called with e as the only argument and will return the result. available. Tostring Demonstrates the tostring global.

globals.name: type
globals.documentation: Returns the type of its only argument, coded as a string. The possible results of this function are "nil" (a string, not the value nil), "number", "string", "boolean", "table", "vector", "function", "thread", "userdata", and "buffer". The buffer and vector primitives are additions from Luau, not from Lua. "table").

globals.name: typeof
globals.documentation: Return the engine-aware type name of a value.

globals.name: unpack
globals.signature: unpack(list: table, i?: int, j?: int): Variant
globals.documentation: Returns the elements from the given list as separate return values, equivalent to list[i], list[i+1], ..., list[j]. By default, i is 1 and j is the length of list (as defined by the # operator). If the range is empty (i > j), no values are returned. An error is raised if the requested range is too large to fit on the stack.

globals.name: UserSettings
globals.documentation: Returns the UserSettings object, which is used to read information from the current user's game menu settings.

globals.name: version
globals.documentation: Returns the current version of Roblox as a string. The integers in the version string are separated by periods, and each integers represent the following, in order: "generation.version.patch.commit".

globals.name: wait
globals.documentation: Deprecated: This method has been superseded by task.wait() and should not be used for future work. Yields the current thread until the specified amount of seconds have elapsed. The delay will have a minimum duration of 29 milliseconds, but this minimum may be higher depending on the target framerate and various throttling conditions. If the seconds parameter is not specified, the minimum duration will be used. This function returns:

globals.name: warn
globals.documentation: Write a warning to the Studio output.

globals.name: workspace
globals.documentation: Convenience reference to the Workspace service.

globals.name: xpcall
globals.signature: xpcall(f: function, err: function, args: Tuple): bool, Variant
globals.documentation: This function is similar to LuaGlobals.pcall(), except that you can set a new error handler. xpcall() calls function f in protected mode, using err as the error handler, and passes a list of arguments. Any error inside f is not propagated; instead, xpcall() catches the error, calls the err function with the original error object, and returns a status code. Its first result is the status code (a boolean), which is true if the call succeeds without errors. In this case, xpcall() also returns all results from the call, after this first result. In case of any error, xpcall() returns false plus the result from err.

globals.name: ypcall
globals.signature: ypcall(f: function, args: Tuple): bool, Variant
globals.documentation: Legacy function to work around an old task scheduling limitation of LuaGlobals.pcall(); should not be used for new work (use LuaGlobals.pcall() instead). failure.

libraries.name: bit32
libraries.documentation: A library of functions to perform bitwise operations.

functions.name: arshift
functions.documentation: Returns the number x shifted disp bits to the right. The number disp may be any representable integer. Negative displacements shift to the left. This shift operation is what is called arithmetic shift. Vacant bits on the left are filled with copies of the higher bit of x; vacant bits on the right are filled with zeros. In particular, displacements with absolute values higher than 31 result in zero or 0xFFFFFFFF (all original bits are shifted out).

functions.name: band
functions.documentation: Returns the bitwise AND of all provided numbers. Each bit is tested against the following truth table: !Bitwise AND of 3 numbers

functions.name: bnot
functions.documentation: Returns the bitwise negation of x. !Negation of a provided number For any integer x, the following identity holds:

functions.name: bor
functions.documentation: Returns the bitwise OR of all provided numbers. Each bit is tested against the following truth table: !Bitwise OR of 3 numbers

functions.name: btest
functions.documentation: Returns true if the bitwise AND of all its operands is different from zero, false otherwise. This is functionally equivalent to bit32.band(...) ~= 0 but returns a boolean directly without the intermediate number. This function is useful for testing whether one or more specific bits are set in a value. For example, you can check whether a particular flag is active in a bitmask: When called with more than two arguments, all values are ANDed together before the zero-test:

functions.name: bxor
functions.documentation: Returns the bitwise XOR of all provided numbers. Each bit is tested against the following truth table: !Bitwise XOR of 3 numbers

functions.name: byteswap
functions.documentation: Reverses the byte order of the 32-bit unsigned integer representation of x. The four bytes are rearranged so that the most-significant byte becomes the least-significant byte and vice versa, converting between big-endian and little-endian representations. This is useful when reading or writing binary data that uses a different byte order (endianness) than expected, such as network protocols or file formats that store multi-byte integers in big-endian order.

functions.name: countlz
functions.documentation: Returns the number of consecutive zero bits in the 32-bit representation of the provided number starting from the left-most (most significant) bit. Returns 32 if the provided number is zero. 32 if n is zero.

functions.name: countrz
functions.documentation: Returns the number of consecutive zero bits in the 32-bit representation of the provided number starting from the right-most (least significant) bit. Returns 32 if the provided number is zero. 32 if n is zero.

functions.name: extract
functions.signature: bit32.extract(n: number, field: number, width?: number): number
functions.documentation: Returns the unsigned number formed by the bits field to field + width - 1 from n. Bits are numbered from 0 (least significant) to 31 (most significant). The default for width is 1. For any valid field and width, this operation is equivalent to bit32.band(bit32.rshift(n, field), 2^width - 1). field must be in the range [0, 31], and width must be in the range [1, 32 - field]. Values outside those ranges raise an error.

functions.name: replace
functions.signature: bit32.replace(n: number, v: number, field: number, width?: number): number
functions.documentation: Returns a copy of n with the bits field to field + width - 1 replaced by the value v. See bit32.extract() for details about field and width.

functions.name: lrotate
functions.documentation: Returns the number x rotated disp bits to the left. The number disp may be any representable integer. For any valid displacement, the following identity holds: In particular, negative displacements rotate to the right.

functions.name: lshift
functions.documentation: Returns the number x shifted disp bits to the left. The number disp may be any representable integer. Negative displacements shift to the right. In any direction, vacant bits are filled with zeros. In particular, displacements with absolute values higher than 31 result in zero (all bits are shifted out). !Number shifted 3 to the left For positive displacements, the following equality holds:

functions.name: rrotate
functions.documentation: Returns the number x rotated disp bits to the right. The number disp may be any representable integer. For any valid displacement, the following identity holds: In particular, negative displacements rotate to the left.

functions.name: rshift
functions.documentation: Returns the number x shifted disp bits to the right. The number disp may be any representable integer. Negative displacements shift to the left. In any direction, vacant bits are filled with zeros. In particular, displacements with absolute values higher than 31 result in zero (all bits are shifted out). !Number shifted 3 to the right For positive displacements, the following equality holds: This shift operation is what is called logical shift.

functions.name: create
functions.documentation: Creates a buffer of the requested size with all bytes initialized to 0. Size limit is 1 GiB, or 1,073,741,824 bytes. Keep in mind that larger buffers might fail to allocate if device is running low on memory.

functions.name: fromstring
functions.documentation: Creates a buffer initialized to the contents of the string. The size of the buffer equals the length of the string.

functions.name: tostring
functions.documentation: Returns the buffer data as a string.

functions.name: len
functions.documentation: Returns the size of the buffer in bytes.

functions.name: readbits
functions.signature: buffer.readbits(b: buffer, bitOffset: number, bitCount: number): number
functions.documentation: Reads a range of bits into an unsigned integer from the buffer based on a specific bitCount integer from 0 to 32, inclusive. For example: Note that 0 bit width is supported only to not error in generalized cases where bit count is dynamic, and reading 0 bits returns 0. Also note that, since the max size of the buffer is 1 GB, bitOffset cannot be handled as a 32‑bit integer number like byte offset in other buffer functions.

functions.name: readi8
functions.documentation: Reads the data from the buffer by reinterpreting bytes at the offset as an 8-bit signed integer and converting it into a number.

functions.name: readu8
functions.documentation: Reads the data from the buffer by reinterpreting bytes at the offset as an 8-bit unsigned integer and converting it into a number.

functions.name: readi16
functions.documentation: Reads the data from the buffer by reinterpreting bytes at the offset as a 16-bit signed integer and converting it into a number.

functions.name: readu16
functions.documentation: Reads the data from the buffer by reinterpreting bytes at the offset as a 16-bit unsigned integer and converting it into a number.

functions.name: readi32
functions.documentation: Reads the data from the buffer by reinterpreting bytes at the offset as a 32-bit signed integer and converting it into a number.

functions.name: readu32
functions.documentation: Reads the data from the buffer by reinterpreting bytes at the offset as a 32-bit unsigned integer and converting it into a number.

functions.name: readf32
functions.documentation: Reads the data from the buffer by reinterpreting bytes at the offset as a 32-bit floating-point value and converting it into a number. If the floating-point value matches any bit patterns that represent NaN (not a number), the returned value may be converted to a different quiet NaN representation.

functions.name: readf64
functions.documentation: Reads the data from the buffer by reinterpreting bytes at the offset as a 64-bit floating-point value and converting it into a number. If the floating-point value matches any bit patterns that represent NaN (not a number), the returned value may be converted to a different quiet NaN representation.

functions.name: writebits
functions.signature: buffer.writebits(b: buffer, bitOffset: number, bitCount: number, value: number): ()
functions.documentation: Writes data to the buffer based on a specific bitCount integer from 0 to 32, inclusive. value is treated as an unsigned 32‑bit number and only bitCount least significant bits are written. Note that 0 bit width is supported only to not error in generalized cases where bit count is dynamic, and writing 0 bits has no effect. Also note that, since the max size of the buffer is 1 GB, bitOffset cannot be handled as a 32‑bit integer number like byte offset in other buffer functions.

functions.name: writei8
functions.signature: buffer.writei8(b: buffer, offset: number, value: number): ()
functions.documentation: Writes data to the buffer by converting the number into an 8-bit signed integer and writing a single byte.

functions.name: writeu8
functions.signature: buffer.writeu8(b: buffer, offset: number, value: number): ()
functions.documentation: Writes data to the buffer by converting the number into an 8-bit unsigned integer and writing a single byte.

functions.name: writei16
functions.signature: buffer.writei16(b: buffer, offset: number, value: number): ()
functions.documentation: Writes data to the buffer by converting the number into a 16-bit signed integer and reinterpreting it as individual bytes.

functions.name: writeu16
functions.signature: buffer.writeu16(b: buffer, offset: number, value: number): ()
functions.documentation: Writes data to the buffer by converting the number into a 16-bit unsigned integer and reinterpreting it as individual bytes.

functions.name: writei32
functions.signature: buffer.writei32(b: buffer, offset: number, value: number): ()
functions.documentation: Writes data to the buffer by converting the number into a 32-bit signed integer and reinterpreting it as individual bytes.

functions.name: writeu32
functions.signature: buffer.writeu32(b: buffer, offset: number, value: number): ()
functions.documentation: Writes data to the buffer by converting the number into a 32-bit unsigned integer and reinterpreting it as individual bytes.

functions.name: writef32
functions.signature: buffer.writef32(b: buffer, offset: number, value: number): ()
functions.documentation: Writes data to the buffer by converting the number into a 32-bit floating-point value and reinterpreting it as individual bytes.

functions.name: writef64
functions.signature: buffer.writef64(b: buffer, offset: number, value: number): ()
functions.documentation: Writes data to the buffer by converting the number into a 64-bit floating-point value and reinterpreting it as individual bytes.

functions.name: readstring
functions.signature: buffer.readstring(b: buffer, offset: number, count: number): string
functions.documentation: Reads a string of length count from the buffer at the specified offset.

functions.name: writestring
functions.signature: buffer.writestring(b: buffer, offset: number, value: string, count: number?): ()
functions.documentation: Writes data from a string into the buffer at the specified offset. If an optional count is specified, only count bytes are taken from the string.

functions.name: copy
functions.signature: buffer.copy(target: buffer, targetOffset: number, source: buffer, sourceOffset?: number?, count: number?): ()
functions.documentation: Copies count bytes from source starting at offset sourceOffset into the target at targetOffset. It's possible for source and target to be the same. Copying an overlapping region inside the same buffer acts as if the source region is copied into a temporary buffer and then that buffer is copied over to the target.

functions.name: fill
functions.signature: buffer.fill(b: buffer, offset: number, value: number, count: number?): ()
functions.documentation: Sets count bytes in the buffer starting at the specified offset to value.

libraries.name: coroutine
libraries.documentation: A function that executes alongside the main thread.

functions.name: Wrapping
functions.documentation: When working with coroutines, you can also forgo the use of the coroutine object and instead use a wrapper function. Such a wrapper function will resume a particular coroutine when it is called and will return only the yielded values. You can do this using coroutine.wrap(): The first value returned from coroutine.resume() describes whether a coroutine ran without errors. However, functions returned by coroutine.wrap() will not do this: instead they directly return the values returned or passed to coroutine.yield(), if any. Should an error have occurred while running the coroutine function, the error is raised on the call of the returned function.

functions.name: Producer
functions.documentation: Imagine a task that produces repetitions of a word: each time it produces a repetition, the next one will produce one more. For example, providing Hello will produce Hello, HelloHello, HelloHelloHello, etc. To do this, you can define repeatThis(): To run this function as a coroutine, you can use coroutine.create() followed by multiple calls to coroutine.resume(): For this producer function, you can also use coroutine.wrap() to get a function that produces values:

functions.name: close
functions.documentation: Closes and puts the provided coroutine in a dead state. This function returns true unless the coroutine is in an error state, in which case it returns false and the error message. A coroutine that is currently running cannot be closed. A coroutine cannot be resumed after it is closed.

functions.name: create
functions.documentation: Creates a new coroutine with body f, which must be a Luau function, and returns it as a thread. The returned coroutine starts in the suspended state and does not begin executing until coroutine.resume() is called on it. The arguments passed to the first coroutine.resume() call are forwarded as the arguments to f.

functions.name: finally
functions.documentation: Registers callback on coroutine co that will be called when co reaches a terminal state. The callback is called with a status string and a set of values: Callbacks run at most once, in reverse registration order (LIFO). When the coroutine reaches a terminal state during the invocation of coroutine.resume() or coroutine.close(), those functions will return only after callbacks complete their work. Callbacks are invoked on the calling thread and may yield. If a callback errors, remaining callbacks in the list are not invoked and false status with the callback error is returned. Attempting to register a callback on a dead coroutine raises an error.

functions.name: isyieldable
functions.documentation: Returns true if the coroutine this function is called within can safely yield. Yielding a coroutine inside metamethods or C functions is prohibited, with the exception of pcall and xpcall.

functions.name: resume
functions.signature: coroutine.resume(co: thread, ...: Variant): bool, Variant<Tuple, string>
functions.documentation: Starts or continues the execution of coroutine co. The first time you resume a coroutine, it starts running its body. The values ... are passed as the arguments to the body function. If the coroutine has yielded, resume restarts it; the values ... are passed as the results from the yield. If the coroutine runs without any errors, resume returns true plus any values passed to yield (if the coroutine yields) or any values returned by the body function (if the coroutine terminates). If there is any error, resume returns false plus the error message. occurred. The values passed to coroutine.yield() or returned by the body function on success, or the error message on failure.

functions.name: running
functions.documentation: Returns the currently running coroutine as a thread value, or nil if called from the main thread. The main thread is not considered a coroutine, so only threads created by coroutine.create() or coroutine.wrap() are returned by this function. thread.

functions.name: status
functions.documentation: Returns the status of coroutine co, as a string: 'running', if the coroutine is running (that is, it called status); 'suspended', if the coroutine is suspended in a call to yield, or if it has not started running yet; 'normal' if the coroutine is active but not running (that is, it has resumed another coroutine); and 'dead' if the coroutine has finished its body function, or if it has stopped with an error.

functions.name: wrap
functions.documentation: Creates a new coroutine, with body f. f must be a Luau function. Returns a function that resumes the coroutine each time it is called. Any arguments passed to the function behave as the extra arguments to resume. Returns the same values returned by resume, except the first boolean. In case of error, propagates the error. returning the yielded or returned values directly (without the boolean status). Raises an error if the coroutine errors.

functions.name: yield
functions.documentation: Suspends the execution of the calling coroutine. Any arguments to yield are passed as extra results to resume. Yielding a coroutine inside metamethods or C functions is prohibited, with the exception of pcall and xpcall. continues this coroutine.

libraries.name: debug
libraries.documentation: This library provides functions useful for debugging and profiling code.

functions.name: traceback
functions.signature: debug.traceback(thread: thread, message: string, level?: number): string
functions.documentation: Returns a traceback of the current function call stack as a string; in other words, a description of the functions that have been called up to this point. During debugging, this behaves like an error stack trace but does not stop execution of the script. The level parameter specifies what level of the call stack to consider, with 1 being the call of debug.traceback() itself, 2 being the call of the function calling debug.traceback(), and so on. See the code sample below for an example of sequential function calls. Note that this function will often return inaccurate results (compared to the original source code) and that the format of the returned traceback may change at any time. You should

functions.name: info
functions.signature: debug.info(thread: thread, level: number, options: string): Tuple
functions.documentation: Allows programmatic inspection of the call stack. This function differs from debug.traceback() in that it guarantees the format of the data it returns. This is useful for general logging and filtering purposes as well as for sending the data to systems expecting structured input, such as crash aggregation. Note that this function is similar to debug.getinfo, an unavailable part of the standard Lua library which serves a similar purpose. identifier (s), line number (l), function name (n), parameter count and whether variadic (a), or the function itself (f).

functions.name: profilebegin
functions.documentation: Starts profiling for a MicroProfiler label.

functions.name: profileend
functions.documentation: Stops profiling for the most recent MicroProfiler label that debug.profilebegin() opened.

functions.name: getmemorycategory
functions.documentation: Returns the name of the current thread's active memory category.

functions.name: setmemorycategory
functions.documentation: Assigns a custom tag name to the current thread's memory category in the Developer Console. Useful for analyzing memory usage of multiple threads in the same script which would otherwise be grouped together under the same tag/name. Returns the name of the current thread's previous memory category.

functions.name: resetmemorycategory
functions.documentation: Resets the tag assigned by debug.setmemorycategory() to the automatically assigned value (typically, the script name).

functions.name: dumpcodesize
functions.documentation: Displays a table of native code size of individual functions and scripts. This function is only available in the Command Bar in Studio. More details can be found on the Native Code Generation page.

functions.name: abs
functions.documentation: Returns the absolute value of x.

functions.name: clamp
functions.signature: math.clamp(x: number, min: number, max: number): number
functions.documentation: Returns a number between min and max, inclusive.

functions.name: max
functions.documentation: Returns the maximum value among the numbers passed to the function.

functions.name: min
functions.documentation: Returns the minimum value among the numbers passed to the function.

functions.name: random
functions.documentation: When called without arguments, returns a uniform pseudo-random real number in the range of 0 to 1 (inclusive of 0 but exclusive of 1). When called with an integer number m, returns a uniform pseudo-random integer in the range of 1 to m, inclusive. When called with two integer numbers m and n, returns a uniform pseudo-random integer in the range of m to n, inclusive. Internally, this uses a 32-bit PCG (Permuted Congruential Generator) which achieves excellent statistical performance and makes its output hard to predict.

functions.name: floor
functions.documentation: Returns the largest integer smaller than or equal to x.

functions.name: ceil
functions.documentation: Returns the smallest integer larger than or equal to x.

functions.name: sqrt
functions.documentation: Returns the square root of x. You can also use the expression x^0.5 to compute this value.

functions.name: acos
functions.documentation: Returns the arc cosine of x.

functions.name: asin
functions.documentation: Returns the arc sine of x.

functions.name: atan
functions.documentation: Returns the arc tangent of x in radians.

functions.name: atan2
functions.documentation: Returns the arc tangent of y/x (in radians) while using the signs of both parameters to find the quadrant of the result. It also handles correctly the case of x being zero.

functions.name: cos
functions.documentation: Returns the cosine of x, assumed to be in radians.

functions.name: cosh
functions.documentation: Returns the hyperbolic cosine of x.

functions.name: deg
functions.documentation: Returns the angle x (given in radians) in degrees.

functions.name: exp
functions.documentation: Returns the value e^x.

functions.name: fmod
functions.documentation: Returns the remainder of the division of x by y that rounds the quotient towards zero.

functions.name: frexp
functions.documentation: Returns m and e such that x = m\*2^e. e is an integer and the absolute value of m is in the range of 0.5 to 1 (inclusive of 0.5 but exclusive of 1), or zero when x is zero. zero. The exponent e such that x = m * 2^e.

functions.name: isfinite
functions.documentation: Returns true if x is a finite number, meaning it is neither NaN nor positive or negative infinity (±math.huge).

functions.name: isinf
functions.documentation: Returns true if x is positive or negative infinity (±math.huge) and false otherwise.

functions.name: isnan
functions.documentation: Returns true if x is not a number (NaN) and false otherwise.

functions.name: ldexp
functions.documentation: Returns x\*2^e (e should be an integer).

functions.name: lerp
functions.signature: math.lerp(a: number, b: number, t: number): number
functions.documentation: Returns the linear interpolation between a and b based on the factor t. This function uses the formula a+(b-a)\*t. t is typically between 0 and 1 but values outside this range are acceptable.

functions.name: log
functions.documentation: Returns the logarithm of x using the given base, or the mathematical constant e if no base is provided (natural logarithm).

functions.name: log10
functions.documentation: Returns the base-10 logarithm of x.

functions.name: map
functions.signature: math.map(x: number, inmin: number, inmax: number, outmin: number, outmax: number): number
functions.documentation: Returns a value that represents x mapped linearly from the input range (inmin to inmax) to the output range (outmin to outmax). This is achieved by determining the relative position of x within the input range and applying that ratio to the output range.

functions.name: modf
functions.documentation: Returns two numbers: the integral part of x and the fractional part of x.

functions.name: noise
functions.signature: math.noise(x: number, y?: number, z?: number): number
functions.documentation: Returns a Perlin noise value. The returned value is most often between the range of -1 to 1 (inclusive) but sometimes may be outside that range; if the interval is critical to you, use math.clamp(noise, -1, 1) on the output. If you leave arguments out, they will be interpreted as zero, so math.noise(1.158) is equivalent to math.noise(1.158, 0, 0) and math.noise(1.158, 5.723) is equivalent to math.noise(1.158, 5.723, 0). Note that this function uses a Perlin noise algorithm to assign fixed values to coordinates. For example, math.noise(1.158, 5.723) will always return 0.48397532105446 and math.noise(1.158, 6) will always return 0.15315161645412.

functions.name: pow
functions.documentation: Returns x^y (you can also use the expression x^y to compute this value).

functions.name: rad
functions.documentation: Returns the angle x (given in degrees) in radians.

functions.name: randomseed
functions.documentation: Sets x as the seed for the pseudo-random generator: equal seeds produce equal sequences of numbers.

functions.name: round
functions.documentation: Returns the integer with the smallest difference between it and the given number. For example, the value 5.8 returns 6. For values like 0.5 that are equidistant to two integers, the value with the greater difference between it and zero is chosen. In other words, the function "rounds away from zero" such that 0.5 rounds to 1 and -0.5 rounds to -1.

functions.name: sign
functions.documentation: Returns -1 if x is less than 0, 0 if x equals 0, or 1 if x is greater than 0. positive.

functions.name: sin
functions.documentation: Returns the sine of x, assumed to be in radians.

functions.name: sinh
functions.documentation: Returns the hyperbolic sine of x.

functions.name: tan
functions.documentation: Returns the tangent of x, assumed to be in radians.

functions.name: tanh
functions.documentation: Returns the hyperbolic tangent of x.

properties.name: e
properties.documentation: Type: number The value of Euler's number, e.

properties.name: huge
properties.documentation: Type: number Returns a value larger than or equal to any other numerical value (about 2<sup>1024</sup>). Dividing a positive number by zero yields this same value.

properties.name: nan
properties.documentation: Type: number A NaN value, as defined by the IEEE 754 standard. Comparing directly to math.nan will always return false; use math.isnan() instead.

properties.name: phi
properties.documentation: Type: number The value of the golden ratio.

properties.name: pi
properties.documentation: Type: number The value of pi.

properties.name: sqrt2
properties.documentation: Type: number The value of the square root of 2.

properties.name: tau
properties.documentation: Type: number The value of tau, which is defined as 2 * math.pi.

libraries.name: os
libraries.documentation: This library provides functions related to time and date.

functions.name: clock
functions.documentation: Returns elapsed time in seconds since an arbitrary baseline with sub-microsecond precision. This function is useful for comparing durations between two events that occur on the same computer, and is the best option for benchmarking. Unlike with functions such as os.time() or DateTime.now(), adjustments to the system clock (such as by the user or NTP) do not cause time to jump forwards or backwards.

functions.name: date
functions.documentation: Formats the given formatString with date/time information based on the given time, or if not provided, the value returned by os.time(). This function should be avoided in new work. Instead, use the DateTime API, which supports localized formatting. The following specifiers (based on the C function strftime) are supported: \* This value can vary depending on the current locale. † The example provided is for February 12th, 2024 (Monday) at 2:14:35 PM (14:14:35), run using locale "en-us" in Pacific Standard Time (PST). If the provided formatString is exactly "*t" (local time) or "!*t" (UTC time), this function instead returns a dictionary containing the following components, which are normally

functions.name: difftime
functions.documentation: Returns the number of seconds from t1 to t2. The difference is computed assuming that t1 and t2 are correctly casted to the time_t format.

functions.name: time
functions.documentation: Returns how many seconds have passed since the Unix epoch (1 January 1970, 00:00:00), under current UTC time. If provided a table formatted similarly to that returned by os.date(), it returns the number of seconds from the Unix epoch to that time instead. Note that the returned time uses the device's local clock. Most operating systems automatically sync their local time against online time servers, so this should be within a few hundred milliseconds. However, users can easily disable sync behavior and set the system time to anything they want; for synchronized time between client and server, use Workspace:GetServerTimeNow() instead.

libraries.name: string

functions.name: find
functions.documentation: Searches for the first occurrence of a pattern in a string and returns the start and end indices of the match. If no match is found, it returns nil. You can specify where to start the search using the optional init parameter which defaults to 1 and can be negative. An optional plain parameter turns off pattern matching, so the function performs a plain substring search; note that if you use plain, you must also provide init.

functions.name: format
functions.documentation: Returns a formatted version of its variable number of arguments following the description given in its first argument, which must be a string. You can convert variables into user-friendly strings of text using the string.format() function. The function requires the following format: %[flags][width].[precision][specifier]. The most important part of string formatting is the specifiers. 3.296E2 | 3e14 | 7FA | When used with e/E and f, forces the output to contain a decimal point, even if no digits would follow (by default, no decimal point is written if no digits follow). When used with g or G, the result is the same as with e or E but trailing zeros are not removed. |

functions.name: gmatch
functions.documentation: Returns an iterator function that, each time it is called, returns the next captures from pattern over the string s. If the pattern has no captures, the whole match is returned on each call. The iterator is typically used in a generic for loop. When the pattern contains capture groups, each call returns the captured substrings as separate values. An empty match (zero-width) advances past the current position by one character to avoid an infinite loop.

functions.name: gsub
functions.signature: string.gsub(s: string, pattern: string, repl: any): (string, number)
functions.documentation: Short for global substitution. Returns a copy of s in which all (or the first n, if given) occurrences of the pattern are substituted (replaced) with the given replacement. The second value returned is the total number of substitutions made. The replacement can be one of several types, each used differently to determine the actual string: An optional final argument can be provided which specifies the maximum number of substitutions to make (for example, stop after 2 replacements)

functions.name: lower
functions.documentation: Returns a copy of the string s with all uppercase ASCII letters (A-Z) changed to their lowercase equivalents (a-z). Characters outside the ASCII letter range, including accented or multibyte characters, are left unchanged.

functions.name: match
functions.documentation: Looks for the first match of pattern in the string s. If the pattern contains captures, the captured substrings are returned as separate values; otherwise, the whole match is returned. If no match is found, the function returns nil. The optional third argument init specifies the byte position to start the search (default 1). A negative init counts from the end of the string. Unlike string.find(), this function returns captured values directly rather than the match indices.

functions.name: sub
functions.signature: string.sub(s: string, i: number, j?: number): string
functions.documentation: Returns the substring of s that starts at byte position i and continues until and including byte position j. Both i and j can be negative: -1 refers to the last byte, -2 to the second-to-last, and so on. The default for i is 1 (the beginning) and j defaults to -1 (the end). If the resolved i is less than 1, it is corrected to 1. If j exceeds the string length, it is corrected to the string length. If after these corrections i is greater than j, the function returns an empty string.

functions.name: upper
functions.documentation: Returns a copy of the string s with all lowercase ASCII letters (a-z) changed to their uppercase equivalents (A-Z). Characters outside the ASCII letter range, including accented or multibyte characters, are left unchanged.

functions.name: byte
functions.signature: string.byte(s: string, i?: number, j?: number): int
functions.documentation: Returns the internal numerical codes of the characters s[i], s[i+1], ..., s[j]. The default value for i is 1; the default value for j is i. These indices are corrected following the same rules of function string.sub(). Numerical codes correspond to single-byte character values (0-255). The function returns one number per character in the specified range, so calling it on a multi-character slice yields multiple return values. If the resolved range is empty (start index greater than end index after adjustment), no values are returned.

functions.name: char
functions.documentation: Receives zero or more integers and returns a string with length equal to the number of arguments, in which each character has the internal numerical code equal to its corresponding argument. Each integer must be in the range [0, 255]; values outside that range raise an error. This is the inverse of string.byte().

functions.name: len
functions.documentation: Returns the number of bytes in the string s. Because Luau strings are byte sequences, this counts bytes rather than Unicode characters or grapheme clusters. An empty string returns 0. Embedded null bytes (\0) are included in the count.

functions.name: pack
functions.documentation: Returns a binary string containing the provided arguments. The first argument, format, determines the way the remaining arguments are packed; see here for options.

functions.name: packsize
functions.documentation: Returns the size in bytes of any string packed with a given description. The sole argument, format, determines the way the remaining arguments are packed, but you cannot use s and z because they have variable lengths. See here for options.

functions.name: rep
functions.documentation: Returns a string that is the concatenation of n copies of the string s. If n is zero or negative, the function returns an empty string. An error is raised if the resulting string would exceed the maximum string size.

functions.name: reverse
functions.documentation: Returns a string that is the string s reversed byte-by-byte. Because the reversal operates on individual bytes, multibyte UTF-8 sequences are not preserved as valid characters after reversal.

functions.name: split
functions.documentation: Splits a string into parts based on the defined separator character(s), returning a table of ordered results. If an empty "slice" is located, that part will be returned as an empty string. For instance string.split("abc||def", "|") will return a table with three strings: "abc", "", and "def". Also note that whitespace from the original string will be preserved, for example string.split("abc _ def", "_") will honor the whitespace on both sides of the _ separator. By default, the separator character is , but you can specify an alternative character or series of characters. Corner Cases

functions.name: unpack
functions.signature: string.unpack(format: string, data: string, readStart?: string): Tuple
functions.documentation: Extracts the values packed in the provided binary string based on the first argument, format, which should match the one originally used to pack() the string; see here for options. The optional third parameter determines the byte at which the reading starts. the first unread byte.

libraries.documentation: Provides generic functions to manipulate strings.

functions.name: clear
functions.documentation: Sets the value for all keys within the given table to nil. This causes the # operator to return 0 for the given table. The allocated capacity of the table's array portion is maintained, which allows for efficient re-use of the space. This function does not delete/destroy the table provided to it. This function is meant to be used specifically for tables that are to be re-used.

functions.name: clone
functions.documentation: Returns an unfrozen shallow copy of the provided table.

functions.name: concat
functions.documentation: Given an array where all elements are strings or numbers, returns the string t[i] ... sep ... t[i+1] ... sep ... t[j]. The default value for sep is an empty string, the default for i is 1, and the default for j is #t. If i is greater than j, returns the empty string.

functions.name: insert
functions.documentation: Appends value to the end of array t at position #t + 1. Unlike the positional overload, no existing elements are shifted, making this the most efficient way to grow an array by one element.

functions.name: move
functions.signature: table.move(a1: {any}, f: number, e: number, t: number, a2?: {any}): {any}
functions.documentation: Copies elements in table src from src[a] up to src[b] into table dst starting at index t. Equivalent to the assignment statement dst[t], ..., dst[t + (b - a)] = src[a], ..., src[b]. The default for dst is src. The destination range may overlap with the source range. Returns dst for convenience.

functions.name: remove
functions.documentation: Removes from array t the element at position pos, returning the value of the removed element. When pos is an integer between 1 and #t, it shifts down the elements t[pos+1], t[pos+2], ..., t[#t] and erases element t[#t]. If the pos parameter is not provided, pos defaults to the length of the table removing the last element. is out of bounds.

functions.name: sort
functions.documentation: Sorts elements of array t in a given order, from t[1] to t[#t]. If comp is given, then it must be a function that receives two elements and returns true when the first element must come before the second in the final order. The error invalid order function for sorting is thrown if both comp(a, b) and comp(b, a) return true. If comp is not given, then the standard Luau operator < is used instead.

functions.name: create
functions.documentation: Creates a table with the array portion allocated to the given number of elements, optionally filled with the given value. If you are inserting into large array-like tables and are certain of a reasonable upper limit to the number of elements, it's recommended to use this function to initialize the table. This ensures the table's array portion of its memory is sufficiently sized, as resizing it can be expensive. For small quantities this is typically not noticeable. filled with value if provided.

functions.name: find
functions.signature: table.find(haystack: table, needle: Variant, init: number): Variant
functions.documentation: Within the given array-like table haystack, find the first occurrence of value needle, starting from index init or the beginning if not provided. If the value is not found, nil is returned. A linear search algorithm is performed. found.

functions.name: freeze
functions.documentation: This function makes the given table read-only, effectively "freezing" it in its current state. Attempting to modify a frozen table throws an error. This freezing effect is shallow, which means that you can write to a table within a frozen table. To deep freeze a table, call this function recursively on all of the descending tables.

functions.name: isfrozen
functions.documentation: This function returns true if the given table is frozen and false if it isn't frozen. You can freeze tables using table.freeze().

functions.name: maxn
functions.documentation: Returns the maximum numeric key of the provided table, or zero if the table has no numeric keys. Gaps in the table are ignored. no numeric keys.

functions.name: pack
functions.documentation: Returns a new table with all arguments stored into keys 1, 2, etc. and with a field "n" with the total number of arguments. Note that the resulting table may not be a sequence. storing the total argument count.

functions.name: unpack
functions.signature: table.unpack(list: table, i?: number, j?: number): Tuple
functions.documentation: Returns the elements from the given list. By default, i is 1 and j is the length of list. Note that this same functionality is also provided by the global LuaGlobals.unpack() function. values.

functions.name: foreach
functions.documentation: Iterates over the provided table, passing the key and value of each iteration over to the provided function. This function has been deprecated and is not recommended for use in new code; use a for loop instead.

functions.name: foreachi
functions.documentation: This is similar to table.foreach() except that index-value pairs are passed, not key-value pairs. This function has been deprecated and is not recommended for use in new code; use a for loop instead.

functions.name: getn
functions.documentation: Returns the number of elements in the table passed. This function has been deprecated and is not recommended for use in new code; use #t instead. operator.

functions.name: wait
functions.documentation: Yield the current thread for at least the requested duration.

functions.name: spawn
functions.documentation: Resume a function or thread immediately through the scheduler.

functions.name: defer
functions.documentation: Schedule a function for the end of the current resumption cycle.

functions.name: delay
functions.documentation: Resume a function after a delay.

functions.name: cancel
functions.documentation: Cancel a scheduled thread.

functions.name: synchronize
functions.documentation: Resume execution in the synchronized phase.

functions.name: desynchronize
functions.documentation: Resume execution in a desynchronized phase when available.

libraries.name: utf8
libraries.documentation: This library provides basic support for UTF-8 encoding.

properties.name: charpattern
properties.documentation: Type: string The pattern "[%z\x01-\x7F\xC2-\xF4][\x80-\xBF]*", which matches exactly zero or more UTF-8 byte sequence, assuming that the subject is a valid UTF-8 string.

functions.name: char
functions.documentation: Receives zero or more codepoints as integers, converts each one to its corresponding UTF-8 byte sequence and returns a string with the concatenation of all these sequences. codepoint.

functions.name: codes
functions.documentation: Returns an iterator function so that the construction: will iterate over all codepoints in string str. It raises an error if it meets any invalid byte sequence. and codepoint of the next character. The input string (passed as the invariant state to the iterator). The initial control value (0) for the iterator.

functions.name: codepoint
functions.signature: utf8.codepoint(str: string, i?: int, j?: int): Tuple<int>
functions.documentation: Returns the codepoints (as integers) from all codepoints in the provided string (str) that start between byte positions i and j (both included). The default for i is 1 and for j is i. It raises an error if it meets any invalid byte sequence. positions i and j.

functions.name: len
functions.signature: utf8.len(s: string, i?: int, j?: int): int
functions.documentation: Returns the number of UTF-8 codepoints in the string _str_ that start between positions i and j (both inclusive). The default for i is 1 and for j is -1. If it finds any invalid byte sequence, returns a nil value plus the position of the first invalid byte. followed by the byte position of the first invalid byte sequence.

functions.name: offset
functions.signature: utf8.offset(s: string, n: int, i?: int): int?
functions.documentation: Returns the position (in bytes) where the encoding of the n‑th codepoint of s (counting from byte position i) starts. A negative n gets characters before position i. The default for i is 1 when n is non-negative and #s + 1 otherwise, so that utf8.offset(s, -n) gets the offset of the n‑th character from the end of the string. If the specified character is neither in the subject nor right after its end, the function returns nil. character is not within the string.

functions.name: graphemes
functions.signature: utf8.graphemes(str: string, i: number, j: number): function
functions.documentation: Returns an iterator function so that will iterate the grapheme clusters of the string. each grapheme cluster.

functions.name: nfcnormalize
functions.documentation: Converts the input string to Normal Form C, which tries to convert decomposed characters into composed characters. their precomposed equivalents.

functions.name: nfdnormalize
functions.documentation: Converts the input string to Normal Form D, which tries to break up composed characters into decomposed characters. their component parts.

properties.name: zero
properties.documentation: Type: vector A pre-allocated constant equivalent to vector.create(0, 0, 0). Useful as a default value or additive identity in vector arithmetic without allocating a new vector each time.

properties.name: one
properties.documentation: Type: vector A pre-allocated constant equivalent to vector.create(1, 1, 1). Useful as a multiplicative identity or scale factor in vector arithmetic without allocating a new vector each time.

functions.name: create
functions.signature: vector.create(x: number, y: number, z: number): vector
functions.documentation: Creates a new vector with the given component values. The z parameter defaults to 0 when omitted, so vector.create(1, 2) is equivalent to vector.create(1, 2, 0).

functions.name: magnitude
functions.documentation: Returns the magnitude (Euclidean length) of the vector, computed as math.sqrt(vec.x^2 + vec.y^2 + vec.z^2).

functions.name: normalize
functions.documentation: Returns a unit vector (magnitude of 1) pointing in the same direction as the input. Computed as vec / vector.magnitude(vec). If the input vector has zero magnitude, the result contains nan components.

functions.name: cross
functions.documentation: Returns the cross product of two vectors, which is a vector perpendicular to both inputs whose magnitude equals the area of the parallelogram they span. The result is computed as vector.create(vec1.y*vec2.z - vec1.z*vec2.y, vec1.z*vec2.x - vec1.x*vec2.z, vec1.x*vec2.y - vec1.y*vec2.x). of the parallelogram they span.

functions.name: dot
functions.documentation: Returns the dot product (scalar product) of two vectors, computed as vec1.x*vec2.x + vec1.y*vec2.y + vec1.z*vec2.z. The result is a single number equal to the product of the magnitudes of the two vectors times the cosine of the angle between them.

functions.name: angle
functions.signature: vector.angle(vec1: vector, vec2: vector, axis: vector?): number
functions.documentation: Computes the angle between two vectors in radians. The axis, if specified, is used to determine the sign of the angle. provided.

functions.name: floor
functions.documentation: Returns a new vector with each component rounded down to the nearest integer, equivalent to vector.create(math.floor(vec.x), math.floor(vec.y), math.floor(vec.z)).

functions.name: ceil
functions.documentation: Returns a new vector with each component rounded up to the nearest integer, equivalent to vector.create(math.ceil(vec.x), math.ceil(vec.y), math.ceil(vec.z)).

functions.name: abs
functions.documentation: Returns a new vector with each component replaced by its absolute value, equivalent to vector.create(math.abs(vec.x), math.abs(vec.y), math.abs(vec.z)).

functions.name: sign
functions.documentation: Returns a new vector where each component is 1 if the corresponding input component is positive, -1 if negative, or 0 if zero. Equivalent to vector.create(math.sign(vec.x), math.sign(vec.y), math.sign(vec.z)). The behavior for negative zero and nan is consistent with math.sign. input component.

functions.name: clamp
functions.signature: vector.clamp(vec: vector, min: vector, max: vector): vector
functions.documentation: Returns a new vector with each component clamped between the corresponding components of min and max. Each component of max must be greater than or equal to the corresponding component of min; otherwise, an error is raised. components of min and max.

functions.name: lerp
functions.signature: vector.lerp(vec1: vector, vec2: vector, alpha: number): vector
functions.documentation: Returns a vector linearly interpolated between two vectors (vec1, vec2) by the fraction alpha. Note that alpha is not limited to the range [0, 1].

functions.name: max
functions.documentation: Returns a new vector where each component is the maximum of the corresponding components across all input vectors. Accepts a variadic number of vectors (at least one). When a component is nan in one vector but a valid number in another, the valid number is used. components across all inputs.

functions.name: min
functions.documentation: Returns a new vector where each component is the minimum of the corresponding components across all input vectors. Accepts a variadic number of vectors (at least one). When a component is nan in one vector but a valid number in another, the valid number is used. components across all inputs.

dataTypes.name: AdReward
dataTypes.documentation: A reward that can be granted to users upon watching rewarded video ads.

dataTypes.name: Axes
dataTypes.documentation: The Axes data type is for the ArcHandles class to control which rotation axes are currently enabled.

constructors.name: new
constructors.documentation: Creates a new Axes from up to 6 Axis or NormalId values. Each NormalId is converted to its corresponding axis (for example, NormalId.Top and NormalId.Bottom both enable the Y axis). Calling Axes.new() with no arguments returns an Axes with all properties set to false.

properties.name: X
properties.documentation: Type: bool Whether the X axis is enabled. Defaults to false when constructed via Axes.new() with no arguments. This property is equivalent to both Left and Right, which also reflect the X axis state.

properties.name: Y
properties.documentation: Type: bool Whether the Y axis is enabled. Defaults to false when constructed via Axes.new() with no arguments. This property is equivalent to both Top and Bottom, which also reflect the Y axis state.

properties.name: Z
properties.documentation: Type: bool Whether the Z axis is enabled. Defaults to false when constructed via Axes.new() with no arguments. This property is equivalent to both Front and Back, which also reflect the Z axis state.

properties.name: Top
properties.documentation: Type: bool Whether the top face is included. This corresponds to the positive Y direction (NormalId.Top) and is always equal to the Y property. Defaults to false.

properties.name: Bottom
properties.documentation: Type: bool Whether the bottom face is included. This corresponds to the negative Y direction (NormalId.Bottom) and is always equal to the Y property. Defaults to false.

properties.name: Left
properties.documentation: Type: bool Whether the left face is included. This corresponds to the negative X direction (NormalId.Left) and is always equal to the X property. Defaults to false.

properties.name: Right
properties.documentation: Type: bool Whether the right face is included. This corresponds to the positive X direction (NormalId.Right) and is always equal to the X property. Defaults to false.

properties.name: Back
properties.documentation: Type: bool Whether the back face is included. This corresponds to the positive Z direction (NormalId.Back) and is always equal to the Z property. Defaults to false.

properties.name: Front
properties.documentation: Type: bool Whether the front face is included. This corresponds to the negative Z direction (NormalId.Front) and is always equal to the Z property. Defaults to false.

dataTypes.name: BrickColor
dataTypes.documentation: A data type that provides a predefined list of named colors.

constructors.name: new
constructors.documentation: Constructs the closest BrickColor that can be matched to the specified Color3. The match uses the same closest-color algorithm as BrickColor.new(r, g, b), comparing the Color3 against every known brick color and returning the one with the smallest total channel distance.

constructors.name: palette
constructors.documentation: Constructs a BrickColor from its zero-based 128-color palette index (Palette Index in color reference table). This is the same palette shown in the Studio color picker. An error is thrown if the index is out of bounds.

constructors.name: random
constructors.documentation: Returns a random BrickColor selected from the 128-color palette. Each call may return a different color.

constructors.name: White
constructors.documentation: Returns the "White" BrickColor.

constructors.name: Gray
constructors.documentation: Returns the "Medium stone grey" BrickColor. This is the same color used as the default when a BrickColor cannot be resolved.

constructors.name: DarkGray
constructors.documentation: Returns the "Dark stone grey" BrickColor.

constructors.name: Black
constructors.documentation: Returns the "Black" BrickColor.

constructors.name: Red
constructors.documentation: Returns the "Bright red" BrickColor.

constructors.name: Yellow
constructors.documentation: Returns the "Bright yellow" BrickColor.

constructors.name: Green
constructors.documentation: Returns the "Dark green" BrickColor.

constructors.name: Blue
constructors.documentation: Returns the "Bright blue" BrickColor.

properties.name: Number
properties.documentation: Type: number The unique number that identifies the BrickColor. This is the same integer used by BrickColor.new() to construct the color and corresponds to the Number column in the color table above. Read-only.

properties.name: r
properties.documentation: Type: number The red component of the BrickColor (between 0 and 1). This is equivalent to BrickColor.Color.R. Read-only.

properties.name: g
properties.documentation: Type: number The green component of the BrickColor (between 0 and 1). This is equivalent to BrickColor.Color.G. Read-only.

properties.name: b
properties.documentation: Type: number The blue component of the BrickColor (between 0 and 1). This is equivalent to BrickColor.Color.B. Read-only.

properties.name: Name
properties.documentation: Type: string The name associated with the BrickColor, for example "Pastel Blue". This is the same string accepted by BrickColor.new(). Read-only.

properties.name: Color
properties.documentation: Type: Color3 The Color3 associated with the BrickColor. The individual components of this value are the same as BrickColor.r, BrickColor.g, and BrickColor.b. Read-only.

dataTypes.name: CatalogSearchParams
dataTypes.documentation: Stores parameters used in catalog searches via AvatarEditorService:SearchCatalogAsync().

properties.name: SearchKeyword
properties.documentation: Type: string The keyword to search for catalog results with.

properties.name: MinPrice
properties.documentation: Type: number The minimum item price to search for. *Default: 0*

properties.name: MaxPrice
properties.documentation: Type: number The maximum item price to search for. *Default: 2147483647*

properties.name: SortType
properties.documentation: Type: CatalogSortType The order in which to sort the results, represented by a CatalogSortType. *Default: Enum.CatalogSortType.Relevance*

properties.name: SortAggregation
properties.documentation: Type: Enum.CatalogSortAggregation The time period to use to aggregate the sort results by, represented by a CatalogSortAggregation. This only applies when the sort type is CatalogSortType.MostFavorited or CatalogSortType.BestSelling. It does not apply for other sort types. *Default: Enum.CatalogSortAggregation.AllTime*

properties.name: CategoryFilter
properties.documentation: Type: CatalogCategoryFilter The category to filter the search by, represented by a CatalogCategoryFilter. *Default: Enum.CatalogCategoryFilter.None*

properties.name: SalesTypeFilter
properties.documentation: Type: Enum.SalesTypeFilter The sales type to filter the search by, represented by a SalesTypeFilter. Use SalesTypeFilter.TimedOptions to return only items that have timed options available. *Default: Enum.SalesTypeFilter.All*

properties.name: BundleTypes
properties.documentation: Type: Array<BundleType> An array containing BundleType values to filter the search by. *Default: {}*

properties.name: AssetTypes
properties.documentation: Type: Array<AvatarAssetType> An array containing AvatarAssetType values to filter the search by.

properties.name: IncludeOffSale
properties.documentation: Type: bool Whether off sale items should be included in the results. *Default: false*

properties.name: CreatorName
properties.documentation: Type: string Search for items with the given creator name. Specify whether to search users, groups, or both with CatalogSearchParams.CreatorType.

properties.name: CreatorType
properties.documentation: Type: Enum.CreatorTypeFilter Search for items created by the given creator type. When unspecified, it defaults to returning creations from both CreatorTypeFilter.User and CreatorTypeFilter.Group. Searching by CatalogSearchParams.CreatorId with CreatorTypeFilter.All results in a HTTP 400 Bad Request error. *Default: Enum.CreatorTypeFilter.All*

properties.name: CreatorId
properties.documentation: Type: number Search for items created by the single creator ID. Specify user or group with CatalogSearchParams.CreatorType. Searching by creator ID and creator name is not supported; specify one, not both. *Default: 0*

properties.name: Limit
properties.documentation: Type: number Specifies the number of items to return. Accepts 10, 28, 30, 60, and 120. Defaults to 30.

dataTypes.name: CFrame

constructors.name: new
constructors.documentation: Creates a CFrame from position (x, y, z) with an orientation specified by the rotation matrix. [[R00 R01 R02] [R10 R11 R12] [R20 R21 R22]]

constructors.name: Angles
constructors.signature: CFrame.Angles(rx: number, ry: number, rz: number): CFrame
constructors.documentation: Equivalent to fromEulerAnglesXYZ().

constructors.name: lookAt
constructors.documentation: Returns a new CFrame with the position of at and facing towards lookAt, optionally specifying the upward direction (up) with a default of (0, 1, 0).

constructors.name: lookAlong
constructors.signature: CFrame.lookAlong(at: Vector3, direction: Vector3, up?: Vector3)
constructors.documentation: Returns a new CFrame with the position of at and facing along direction, optionally specifying the upward direction (up) with a default of (0, 1, 0). This constructor is equivalent to CFrame.lookAt(at, at + direction).

constructors.name: fromRotationBetweenVectors
constructors.documentation: Returns a CFrame whose rotation represents the shortest-arc rotation that aligns vector from with vector to. The input vectors do not need to be unit length; they are normalized internally. The resulting CFrame has its position set to (0, 0, 0).

constructors.name: fromEulerAngles
constructors.signature: CFrame.fromEulerAngles(rx: number, ry: number, rz: number, order?: RotationOrder)
constructors.documentation: Returns a rotated CFrame from angles rx, ry, and rz in radians. Rotations are applied in the optional RotationOrder with a default of XYZ, equivalent to:

constructors.name: fromEulerAnglesXYZ
constructors.signature: CFrame.fromEulerAnglesXYZ(rx: number, ry: number, rz: number)
constructors.documentation: Returns a rotated CFrame from angles rx, ry, and rz in radians using RotationOrder.XYZ, equivalent to:

constructors.name: fromEulerAnglesYXZ
constructors.signature: CFrame.fromEulerAnglesYXZ(rx: number, ry: number, rz: number)
constructors.documentation: Returns a rotated CFrame from angles rx, ry, and rz in radians using RotationOrder.YXZ, equivalent to:

constructors.name: fromOrientation
constructors.signature: CFrame.fromOrientation(rx: number, ry: number, rz: number)
constructors.documentation: Equivalent to fromEulerAnglesYXZ().

constructors.name: fromAxisAngle
constructors.documentation: Returns a CFrame rotated r radians around the axis v. The axis vector is normalized internally, so it does not need to be unit length. The resulting CFrame has no translation (position is (0, 0, 0)). A positive angle represents a counter-clockwise rotation when looking from the tip of the axis vector toward the origin (right-hand rule).

constructors.name: fromMatrix
constructors.signature: CFrame.fromMatrix(pos: Vector3, vX: Vector3, vY: Vector3, vZ: Vector3)
