constructors.documentation: Returns a CFrame from a translation and the columns of a rotation matrix. If vZ is excluded, the third column is calculated as vX:Cross(vY).Unit.

properties.name: Position
properties.documentation: Type: Vector3 The positional component of the CFrame as a Vector3. Equivalent to Vector3.new(cf.X, cf.Y, cf.Z).

properties.name: LookVector
properties.documentation: Type: Vector3 The forward-direction component of the CFrame object's orientation, equivalent to the negated ZVector or the negated third column of the rotation matrix. Adding a CFrame object's LookVector to itself produces a CFrame moved forward in whichever direction it's facing by 1 unit.

properties.name: Rotation
properties.documentation: Type: CFrame A copy of the CFrame with the positional component set to (0, 0, 0), retaining only the rotational component. Useful for isolating a CFrame object's orientation independent of its position.

properties.name: X
properties.documentation: Type: number The X component of the CFrame object's world-space position. Equivalent to CFrame.Position.X.

properties.name: Y
properties.documentation: Type: number The Y component of the CFrame object's world-space position. Equivalent to CFrame.Position.Y.

properties.name: Z
properties.documentation: Type: number The Z component of the CFrame object's world-space position. Equivalent to CFrame.Position.Z.

properties.name: RightVector
properties.documentation: Type: Vector3 The right-direction component of the CFrame object's orientation. Equivalent to XVector or the first column of the rotation matrix.

properties.name: UpVector
properties.documentation: Type: Vector3 The up-direction component of the CFrame object's orientation. Equivalent to YVector or the second column of the rotation matrix.

properties.name: XVector
properties.documentation: Type: Vector3 The X component of the CFrame object's orientation. Equivalent to RightVector or the first column of the rotation matrix.

properties.name: YVector
properties.documentation: Type: Vector3 The Y component of the CFrame object's orientation. Equivalent to UpVector or the second column of the rotation matrix.

properties.name: ZVector
properties.documentation: Type: Vector3 The Z component of the CFrame object's orientation. Equivalent to the negated LookVector or the third column of the rotation matrix.

methods.name: Lerp
methods.documentation: Returns a CFrame interpolated between itself and goal by the fraction alpha. The positional component is interpolated linearly while the rotational component is interpolated using spherical linear interpolation (slerp), producing a constant-speed rotation along the shortest arc. An alpha of 0 returns the original CFrame and an alpha of 1 returns goal.

methods.name: ToWorldSpace
methods.documentation: Receives one or more CFrame objects and returns them transformed from object to world space. Equivalent to: CFrame * cf

methods.name: Inverse
methods.documentation: Returns the inverse of the CFrame, representing the transformation that undoes the original. For any CFrame cf, the expression cf * cf:Inverse() produces the identity CFrame. The inverse reverses both the rotation (transposing the rotation matrix) and the translation.

methods.name: Orthonormalize
methods.documentation: Returns an orthonormalized copy of the CFrame. The BasePart.CFrame property automatically applies orthonormalization, but other APIs which take CFrames do not, so this method is occasionally necessary when incrementally updating a CFrame and using it with them.

methods.name: ToObjectSpace
methods.documentation: Receives one or more CFrame objects and returns them transformed from world to object space. Equivalent to: CFrame:Inverse() * cf

methods.name: PointToWorldSpace
methods.documentation: Receives one or more Vector3 objects and returns them transformed from object to world space. Equivalent to: CFrame * v3

methods.name: PointToObjectSpace
methods.documentation: Receives one or more Vector3 objects and returns them transformed from world to object space. Equivalent to: CFrame:Inverse() * v3

methods.name: VectorToWorldSpace
methods.documentation: Receives one or more Vector3 objects and returns them rotated from object to world space. Equivalent to: (CFrame - CFrame.Position) * v3

methods.name: VectorToObjectSpace
methods.documentation: Receives one or more Vector3 objects and returns them rotated from world to object space. Equivalent to: (CFrame:Inverse() - CFrame:Inverse().Position) * v3

methods.name: GetComponents
methods.documentation: Returns the 12 numeric components of the CFrame as a tuple: x, y, z (position), followed by R00, R01, R02, R10, R11, R12, R20, R21, R22 (the 3×3 rotation matrix in row-major order). This is the reverse of the 12-argument CFrame.new() constructor. R21, R22.

methods.name: ToEulerAngles
methods.documentation: Returns approximate angles that could be used to generate the CFrame using the optional RotationOrder. If you don't provide order, the method uses RotationOrder.XYZ.

methods.name: ToEulerAnglesXYZ
methods.documentation: Returns the approximate angles, in radians, that could be used to generate the CFrame using RotationOrder.XYZ. The three returned values represent rotations around the X, Y, and Z axes respectively. Due to the nature of Euler angle decomposition, the angles are approximate and subject to gimbal lock near pitch angles of ±90 degrees.

methods.name: ToEulerAnglesYXZ
methods.documentation: Returns the approximate angles, in radians, that could be used to generate the CFrame using RotationOrder.YXZ. The three returned values represent rotations around the X, Y, and Z axes respectively. Due to the nature of Euler angle decomposition, the angles are approximate and subject to gimbal lock near pitch angles of ±90 degrees.

methods.name: ToOrientation
methods.documentation: Returns the approximate angles, in radians, that could be used to generate the CFrame using RotationOrder.YXZ. Equivalent to CFrame:ToEulerAnglesYXZ().

methods.name: ToAxisAngle
methods.documentation: Returns a unit Vector3 representing the axis of rotation and a number representing the angle of rotation in radians. A positive angle represents counter-clockwise rotation when looking from the tip of the axis vector toward the origin (right-hand rule). This is the inverse of CFrame.fromAxisAngle().

methods.name: components
methods.documentation: Equivalent to CFrame:GetComponents(). R21, R22.

methods.name: FuzzyEq
methods.documentation: Returns true if the other CFrame is sufficiently close to this CFrame in both position and rotation. The epsilon value is used to control the tolerance for this similarity; this value is optional and should be a small positive value if provided. The similarity for position is component-wise while rotation uses a fast approximation of the angle difference.

methods.name: AngleBetween
methods.documentation: Returns the angle, in radians, between the orientation of one CFrame and another. This function does not take the position of either CFrame into account and only looks at the relative orientation. pi].

dataTypes.documentation: A data type that represents both a 3D position and orientation.

constants.name: identity
constants.documentation: An identity CFrame with no translation or rotation.

dataTypes.name: Collection
dataTypes.documentation: A live, query-based group of instances returned by CollectionService:CreateCollection().

properties.name: Enabled
properties.documentation: Type: bool Defaults to true. Setting this to false fires OnRemoved for every instance currently in the collection and stops all of its callbacks. Setting it back to true re-evaluates the query and fires OnAdded again for every matching instance. Assigning a non-boolean value raises an error.

methods.name: ForEach
methods.documentation: Iterates over the instances currently in the collection, calling callback with each one. ForEach() operates on a snapshot taken at call time, so it is safe to add, remove, or destroy instances from within the callback; instances that begin matching during iteration are not visited. Calling ForEach() after the collection has been destroyed raises an error.

methods.name: Destroy
methods.documentation: Stops firing the collection's callbacks, releases the connections it manages on its members, and empties its set of instances. After a collection is destroyed, calling ForEach() raises an error. A collection is also destroyed automatically when the root passed to CreateCollection() is destroyed.

dataTypes.name: Color3

constructors.name: new
constructors.signature: Color3.new(r: number, g: number, b: number): Color3
constructors.documentation: Returns a Color3 with the given red, green, and blue values. The parameters should be within the range of 0 to 1.

constructors.name: fromRGB
constructors.signature: Color3.fromRGB(r: number, g: number, b: number): Color3
constructors.documentation: Creates a Color3 with the given red, green, and blue components. Unlike most other Color3 functions, the parameters for this function should be within the range of 0 to 255.

constructors.name: fromHSV
constructors.signature: Color3.fromHSV(h: number, s: number, v: number): Color3
constructors.documentation: Creates a Color3 with the given hue, saturation, and value. The parameters should be within the range of 0 to 1.

constructors.name: fromHex
constructors.documentation: Returns a new Color3 from a six- or three-character hexadecimal format, case insensitive. A preceding hashtag (#) is ignored, if present. This function interprets the given string as a typical web hex color in the format RRGGBB or RGB (shorthand for RRGGBB). For example, #FFAA00 produces an orange color and is the same as #FA0.

properties.name: R
properties.documentation: Type: number The red value of the color.

properties.name: G
properties.documentation: Type: number The green value of the color.

properties.name: B
properties.documentation: Type: number The blue value of the color.

methods.name: Lerp
methods.documentation: Returns a Color3 interpolated between two colors. The alpha value should be within the range of 0 to 1.

methods.name: ToHSV
methods.documentation: Returns the hue, saturation, and value of a Color3. This function is the inverse operation of the Color3.fromHSV() constructor.

methods.name: ToHex
methods.documentation: Converts the color to a six-character hexadecimal string representing the color in the format RRGGBB. It is not prefixed with an octothorpe (#). The returned string can be provided to Color3.fromHex() to produce the original color.

methods.name: toHSV
methods.documentation: Returns the hue, saturation, and value of a Color3. This function is the inverse operation of the Color3.fromHSV() constructor.

dataTypes.documentation: A color value comprised of red, green, and blue components.

dataTypes.name: ColorSequence
dataTypes.documentation: A gradient of color values comprised of ColorSequenceKeypoints.

constructors.name: new
constructors.documentation: Returns a new ColorSequence from an array of ColorSequenceKeypoints. The keypoints must be in a non-descending time value order. At least two keypoints must be provided, and they must have a time value of 0 (first) and 1 (last).

properties.name: Keypoints
properties.documentation: Type: Array An array containing ColorSequenceKeypoint values for the ColorSequence.

dataTypes.name: ColorSequenceKeypoint
dataTypes.documentation: A color and time value that represents a keypoint in a ColorSequence.

constructors.name: new
constructors.documentation: Returns a ColorSequenceKeypoint with the given time and color. The time parameter should be a number between 0 and 1, where 0 represents the beginning of the sequence and 1 represents the end. The color parameter is a Color3 whose components must each be between 0 and 1.

properties.name: Time
properties.documentation: Type: number The relative time at which this keypoint is positioned within the parent ColorSequence, expressed as a number from 0 to 1 where 0 is the beginning of the sequence and 1 is the end. Within a ColorSequence, the first keypoint must have a time of 0 and the last keypoint must have a time of 1; any intermediate keypoints must be in ascending time order. The engine linearly interpolates colors between consecutive keypoints in RGB color space based on their time positions. Defaults to 0.

properties.name: Value
properties.documentation: Type: Color3 The Color3 color value at this keypoint's position in the sequence. When the engine evaluates a ColorSequence, it linearly interpolates between adjacent keypoints' color values in RGB color space based on time. Each component of the color (red, green, blue) must be between 0 and 1. Defaults to (0, 0, 0) (black).

dataTypes.name: Content
dataTypes.documentation: Represents a reference to asset content stored externally or as an object within the place.

constructors.name: fromUri
constructors.documentation: Returns a new Content with an asset URI string value referencing content external to the place. Content.SourceType will be Uri, and Content.Uri will contain a non‑nil string value. If uri is empty, Content.none will be returned instead.

constructors.name: fromAssetId
constructors.documentation: Returns a new Content from a numeric asset ID. This is a convenience constructor equivalent to calling Content.fromUri("rbxassetid://" .. tostring(assetId)). Content.SourceType will be Uri, and Content.Uri will contain the formatted rbxassetid:// URI string. If assetId is 0, Content.none will be returned instead. Throws if assetId is non‑finite, for example math.huge() or 0/0.

constructors.name: fromObject
constructors.documentation: Returns a new Content with a strong reference to an Object. Content.SourceType will be Object, and Content.Object will contain a non‑nil Object reference. Content.Object references are strong references that hold shared ownership of the Object. Any Content.Object reference will extend the lifetime of that Object and prevent it from being garbage collected. Throws if object is nil.

constants.name: none
constants.documentation: An empty Content value with Content.SourceType of None.

properties.name: SourceType
properties.documentation: Type: Enum.ContentSourceType The source type of the contained value. Indicates which property contains a non‑nil value.

properties.name: Uri
properties.documentation: Type: string? A URI string if Content.SourceType is Uri, otherwise nil.

properties.name: Object
properties.documentation: Type: Object? A reference to a non-nil Object if Content.SourceType is Object, otherwise nil.

properties.name: Opaque
properties.documentation: Type: Opaque? A reference to a non-nil Opaque content if Content.SourceType is Opaque, otherwise nil.

dataTypes.name: DateTime
dataTypes.documentation: A data type that represents a moment in time.

constructors.name: now
constructors.documentation: Returns a new DateTime representing the current moment in time, using the device's local clock. Most operating systems automatically sync their local time against online time servers, so this should be within a few hundred milliseconds. However, users can easily disable sync behavior and set the system time to anything they want; for synchronized time between client and server, use Workspace:GetServerTimeNow() instead. When you need to precisely measure the time elapsed between two points in time, like when testing performance, use os.clock() instead.

constructors.name: fromUnixTimestamp
constructors.documentation: Returns a new DateTime object from the given Unix timestamp, or the number of seconds since January 1st, 1970 at 00:00 (UTC). This function only has granularity to 1 second. To represent sub-second timestamps, use DateTime.fromUnixTimestampMillis() instead.

constructors.name: fromUnixTimestampMillis
constructors.documentation: Returns a new DateTime object from the given Unix timestamp, or the number of milliseconds since January 1st, 1970 at 00:00 (UTC).

constructors.name: fromUniversalTime
constructors.signature: DateTime.fromUniversalTime(year?: number, month?: number, day?: number, hour?: number, minute?: number, second?: number, millisecond?: number)
constructors.documentation: Returns a new DateTime using the given units from a UTC time. The values accepted are similar to those found in the time value table returned by ToUniversalTime().

constructors.name: fromLocalTime
constructors.signature: DateTime.fromLocalTime(year?: number, month?: number, day?: number, hour?: number, minute?: number, second?: number, millisecond?: number)
constructors.documentation: Returns a new DateTime using the given units from a local time. The values accepted are similar to those found in the time value table returned by ToLocalTime().

constructors.name: fromIsoDate
constructors.documentation: Returns a DateTime from an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC time, such as those returned by ToIsoDate(). If the string parsing fails, the function returns nil. An example ISO 8601 date-time string would be 2020-01-02T10:30:45Z, which represents January 2nd 2020 at 10:30 AM, 45 seconds.

properties.name: UnixTimestamp
properties.documentation: Type: number The number of seconds since January 1st, 1970 at 00:00 UTC (the Unix epoch). Range is -17,987,443,200 to 253,402,300,799, approximately years 1400–9999.

properties.name: UnixTimestampMillis
properties.documentation: Type: number The number of milliseconds since January 1st, 1970 at 00:00 UTC (the Unix epoch). Range is -17,987,443,200,000 to 253,402,300,799,999, approximately years 1400–9999.

methods.name: ToUniversalTime
methods.documentation: Converts the value of this DateTime object to Universal Coordinated Time (UTC). The returned table contains the following keys: Year, Month, Day, Hour, Minute, Second, Millisecond. For more details, see the time value table in this data type's description. The values within this table could be passed to fromUniversalTime() to produce the original DateTime object.

methods.name: ToLocalTime
methods.documentation: Converts the value of this DateTime object to local time. The returned table contains the following keys: Year, Month, Day, Hour, Minute, Second, Millisecond. For more details, see the time value table in this data type's description. The values within this table could be passed to fromLocalTime() to produce the original DateTime object.

methods.name: ToIsoDate
methods.documentation: Formats a date as a ISO 8601 date-time string. The value returned by this function could be passed to fromIsoDate() to produce the original DateTime object. An example ISO 8601 date-time string would be 2020-01-02T10:30:45Z, which represents January 2nd 2020 at 10:30 AM, 45 seconds.

methods.name: FormatUniversalTime
methods.documentation: Generates a string from the DateTime value interpreted as Universal Coordinated Time (UTC) and a format string. The format string should contain tokens, which will replace to certain date/time values described by the DateTime object. For more details, see the String Format section in this data type's description.

methods.name: FormatLocalTime
methods.documentation: Generates a string from the DateTime value interpreted as local time and a format string. The format string should contain tokens, which will replace to certain date/time values described by the DateTime object. For more details, see the String Format section in this data type's description.

dataTypes.name: DockWidgetPluginGuiInfo
dataTypes.documentation: Describes details for a DockWidgetPluginGui.

constructors.name: new
constructors.signature: DockWidgetPluginGuiInfo.new(InitialDockState?: InitialDockState, InitialEnabled?: bool, InitialEnabledShouldOverrideRestore?: bool, FloatingXSize?: number, FloatingYSize?: number, MinWidth?: number, MinHeight?: number)
constructors.documentation: The main constructor function for the DockWidgetPluginGuiInfo.

properties.name: InitialEnabled
properties.documentation: Type: bool The initial enabled state of a PluginGui created using this DockWidgetPluginGuiInfo. If a PluginGui with the same ''pluginGuiId'' has previously been created in an earlier session of Roblox Studio, then it will reload that saved enabled state (unless InitialEnabledShouldOverrideRestore is true).

properties.name: InitialEnabledShouldOverrideRestore
properties.documentation: Type: bool If true, the value of InitialEnabled will override the previously saved enabled state of a PluginGui being created with this DockWidgetPluginGuiInfo. The previously saved enabled state is loaded based on the pluginGuiId argument of Plugin:CreateDockWidgetPluginGuiAsync().

properties.name: FloatingXSize
properties.documentation: Type: number The initial pixel width of a PluginGui created using this DockWidgetPluginGuiInfo, when the InitialDockState is set to Float.

properties.name: FloatingYSize
properties.documentation: Type: number The initial pixel height of a PluginGui created using this DockWidgetPluginGuiInfo, when the InitialDockState is set to Float.

properties.name: MinWidth
properties.documentation: Type: number The minimum width of a PluginGui created using this DockWidgetPluginGuiInfo, in pixels. Each platform has its own absolute minimum that Roblox will enforce. These variations exist to account for the contents of the title bar (which varies by platform) when the widget is floating. For example, on a Mac, the width can never be less than ~80 pixels to accommodate the close/minimize/maximize buttons.

properties.name: MinHeight
properties.documentation: Type: number The minimum height of a PluginGui created using this DockWidgetPluginGuiInfo, in pixels.

dataTypes.name: Faces
dataTypes.documentation: A data type containing six booleans, each representing a face of a BasePart.

constructors.name: new
constructors.documentation: Creates a new Faces given some number of NormalId as arguments. Each NormalId provided indicates the property of the same name in the new Faces will be true.

properties.name: Top
properties.documentation: Type: bool Whether the top face (positive Y direction, corresponding to NormalId.Top) is included in this Faces value. Defaults to false when NormalId.Top is not passed to the Faces.new() constructor.

properties.name: Bottom
properties.documentation: Type: bool Whether the bottom face (negative Y direction, corresponding to NormalId.Bottom) is included in this Faces value. Defaults to false when NormalId.Bottom is not passed to the Faces.new() constructor.

properties.name: Left
properties.documentation: Type: bool Whether the left face (negative X direction, corresponding to NormalId.Left) is included in this Faces value. Defaults to false when NormalId.Left is not passed to the Faces.new() constructor.

properties.name: Right
properties.documentation: Type: bool Whether the right face (positive X direction, corresponding to NormalId.Right) is included in this Faces value. Defaults to false when NormalId.Right is not passed to the Faces.new() constructor.

properties.name: Back
properties.documentation: Type: bool Whether the back face (positive Z direction, corresponding to NormalId.Back) is included in this Faces value. Defaults to false when NormalId.Back is not passed to the Faces.new() constructor.

properties.name: Front
properties.documentation: Type: bool Whether the front face (negative Z direction, corresponding to NormalId.Front) is included in this Faces value. Defaults to false when NormalId.Front is not passed to the Faces.new() constructor.

dataTypes.name: FloatCurveKey
dataTypes.documentation: A time-value pair used with FloatCurve instances.

constructors.name: new
constructors.signature: FloatCurveKey.new(time: number, value: number, Interpolation: KeyInterpolationMode)
constructors.documentation: Creates a new FloatCurveKey at a given time and value. LeftTangent and RightTangent are left uninitialized and, if not initialized, tangent values of 0 will be used when evaluating the curve.

properties.name: Interpolation
properties.documentation: Type: KeyInterpolationMode Specifies the interpolation mode used for the curve segment that begins at this key and ends at the next key on the FloatCurve. Each segment of the curve can use a different interpolation mode. The default value is KeyInterpolationMode.Cubic. The available modes are: Changing this property to a non-cubic mode automatically clears the RightTangent of this key, because only cubic segments use a right tangent.

properties.name: Time
properties.documentation: Type: number The time position of this FloatCurveKey along the curve's timeline. The default value is 0. Keys within a FloatCurve are kept sorted in ascending time order; if you insert a key at a time that already exists on the curve, the existing key at that time is replaced.

properties.name: Value
properties.documentation: Type: number The numerical output value at this key's position on the curve. The default value is 0. When a FloatCurve is sampled at this key's Time, the curve evaluates to this value (subject to any interpolation with neighboring keys depending on the sampling time).

properties.name: RightTangent
properties.documentation: Type: number The slope of the curve leaving this key toward the next key. The default value is nil, which means the tangent is automatically computed (an effective value of 0 is used during evaluation). This property can only be set when Interpolation is KeyInterpolationMode.Cubic; attempting to set it on a key with Constant or Linear interpolation raises a runtime error. Pairing a different RightTangent value on this key with a different LeftTangent value on the next key creates a discontinuity in slope (a "corner") at the next key.

properties.name: LeftTangent
properties.documentation: Type: number The slope of the curve arriving at this key from the previous key. The default value is nil, which means the tangent is automatically computed (an effective value of 0 is used during evaluation). Unlike RightTangent, this property can be set on a key with any interpolation mode, because the preceding segment may itself use cubic interpolation and therefore needs a defined left tangent at this endpoint.

dataTypes.name: Font
dataTypes.documentation: Describes the font used to render text.

constructors.name: new
constructors.signature: Font.new(family: Content, weight?: FontWeight, style?: FontStyle)
constructors.documentation: Creates a new Font. Font.new() Shows how to use Font.new().

constructors.name: fromEnum
constructors.documentation: Creates a Font from an Font value. Throws an error when called with Font.Unknown. The following table indicates how each Font value maps to a font Family. Font.fromEnum() Shows how to use Font.fromEnum().

constructors.name: fromName
constructors.signature: Font.fromName(name: string, weight?: FontWeight, style?: FontStyle)
constructors.documentation: This is a convenience method for creating fonts from the content folder. The name you pass in will be converted into an asset ID like rbxasset://fonts/families/BuilderSans.json. The name can only contain alphabetical characters, digits, _ (underscore), and - (hyphen). It can't contain any spaces. Font.fromName() Shows how to use Font.fromName().

constructors.name: fromId
constructors.signature: Font.fromId(id: number, weight?: FontWeight, style?: FontStyle)
constructors.documentation: This is a convenience method for creating fonts from an asset ID number. Font.fromId() Shows how to use Font.fromId().

properties.name: Family
properties.documentation: Type: Content The asset ID for the font family. These start with either rbxasset:// or rbxassetid://.

properties.name: Weight
properties.documentation: Type: FontWeight How thick the text is. The default value is FontWeight.Regular. When set, Font.Bold is updated and becomes true if the weight is FontWeight.SemiBold or thicker.

properties.name: Style
properties.documentation: Type: FontStyle Whether the font is italic. The default value is FontStyle.Normal.

properties.name: Bold
properties.documentation: Type: bool Whether the font is bold. Sets Font.Weight to FontWeight.Bold when true, or to FontWeight.Regular otherwise.

dataTypes.name: Instance
dataTypes.documentation: Holds the constructor for Instances.

constructors.name: new
constructors.documentation: Creates a new Instance of type className. Abstract classes and services cannot be created with this constructor. Note that when the Parent of an object is set, Luau listens to a variety of different property changes for replication, rendering, and physics. For performance reasons, it's recommended to set the instance's Parent property last when creating new objects, instead of specifying the second argument (parent) of this constructor.

constructors.name: fromExisting
constructors.documentation: Creates a new object with the same type and property values as an existing object. In most cases using Instance:Clone() is more appropriate, but this constructor is useful when implementing low‑level libraries or systems. There are two behavioral differences between this constructor and the Instance:Clone() method:

dataTypes.name: InstanceHandle
dataTypes.documentation: A lightweight, weak reference to an Instance that might not be available locally.

constructors.name: new
constructors.documentation: The handle refers to the instance weakly and doesn't extend its lifetime. Throws if instance is neither an Instance nor nil.

methods.name: Get
methods.documentation: This method doesn't yield. Get() returns nil when the handle is empty, when the target hasn't arrived on the client or server running the script, when the target is no longer available after streaming out, when the target has been garbage collected, and when the target isn't accessible to the calling script. Use InstanceHandle:Wait() to yield until the target arrives instead of checking once.

methods.name: Wait
methods.documentation: Returns nil if the handle is empty, the target is inaccessible to the calling script, or timeout elapses first. Wait() returns immediately when the target is already available and when the handle is empty. Pass a timeout whenever you can't guarantee that the target reaches the caller. A target that's destroyed before it replicates leaves a handle that never resolves, and a Wait() with no timeout never returns. A pending wait can't be cancelled: task.cancel() stops your coroutine, but the wait isn't unregistered until the target arrives or the timeout elapses. timeout must be a number greater than zero. Throws if timeout is zero, negative, or not a number.

dataTypes.name: NumberRange
dataTypes.documentation: Represents a range of numbers.

constructors.name: new
constructors.documentation: Returns a new NumberRange with the provided minimum and maximum. The minimum must be less than or equal to maximum.

properties.name: Min
properties.documentation: Type: number The minimum value of the NumberRange, always less than or equal to the maximum.

properties.name: Max
properties.documentation: Type: number The maximum value of the NumberRange, always greater than or equal to the minimum.

dataTypes.name: NumberSequence
dataTypes.documentation: A series of floats across a period of time.

constructors.name: new
constructors.documentation: Returns a NumberSequence from an array of NumberSequenceKeypoints. The keypoints must be provided in a non-descending time value order. At least two keypoints must be provided, and they must have a time value of 0 (first) and 1 (last).

properties.name: Keypoints
properties.documentation: Type: Array An array containing NumberSequenceKeypoint values for the NumberSequence.

dataTypes.name: NumberSequenceKeypoint
dataTypes.documentation: Represents keypoint within a NumberSequence with a particular time, value, and envelope size.

constructors.name: new
constructors.signature: NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(time: number, value: number, envelope: number)
constructors.documentation: Returns a NumberSequenceKeypoint with the given time, value, and envelope. The envelope parameter must be a non-negative number that defines the amount of random variance applied to value at runtime; the actual output for this keypoint is chosen randomly within [value − envelope, value + envelope].

properties.name: Envelope
properties.documentation: Type: number The amount of variance allowed from the value. For example, a value of 0.5 with an envelope of 0.1 could compute to between 0.4 and 0.6 at runtime. The most common use case for this property is to randomize the size of particles (within the envelope) from a ParticleEmitter.

properties.name: Time
properties.documentation: Type: number The relative time at which this keypoint is positioned within the parent NumberSequence, expressed as a number from 0 to 1 where 0 is the beginning of the sequence and 1 is the end. Within a NumberSequence, the first keypoint must have a time of 0 and the last keypoint must have a time of 1; any intermediate keypoints must be in ascending time order. The engine linearly interpolates values and envelopes between consecutive keypoints based on their time positions. Defaults to 0.

properties.name: Value
properties.documentation: Type: number The base numeric value at this keypoint's position in the sequence. When the engine evaluates a NumberSequence, it linearly interpolates between adjacent keypoints' values based on time. If Envelope is greater than 0, the actual output at runtime may vary randomly within the range [Value − Envelope, Value + Envelope]. Defaults to 0.

dataTypes.name: OverlapParams
dataTypes.documentation: Stores parameters used in boundary-querying functions.

constructors.name: new
constructors.documentation: Returns a blank OverlapParams object. Unlike other data type constructors, this constructor does not have any parameters, so you should set its properties appropriately.

properties.name: ExcludeInstances
properties.documentation: Type: {Instance}? An optional array of instances whose descendants will be excluded from the query. This property can be used simultaneously with IncludeInstances to allow for mixed filtering, for example including a large folder but excluding specific child instances. If an instance matches both an exclude and include filter, exclusions take priority over inclusions.

properties.name: IncludeInstances
properties.documentation: Type: {Instance}? An optional array of instances whose descendants will be included in the query. This property can be used simultaneously with ExcludeInstances to allow for mixed filtering. If an instance matches both an exclude and include filter, exclusions take priority over inclusions. Setting IncludeInstances to nil versus an empty array ({}) has opposite effects. IncludeInstances = nil is the most permissive filter (includes everything), whereas IncludeInstances = {} is the most restrictive filter (includes nothing).

properties.name: MaxParts
properties.documentation: Type: number The maximum amount of parts to be returned by the query. The default value of zero (0) represents no limit.

properties.name: CollisionGroup
properties.documentation: Type: string Specifies a collision group for the operation. Parts in collision groups that are set to not collide with this group are ignored. If this property is omitted, the operation assumes the Default collision group.

properties.name: Tolerance
properties.documentation: Type: number Slightly increases the volume of the boundary-querying operation, clamped between 0 and 0.05 studs.

properties.name: RespectCanCollide
properties.documentation: Type: bool This property, if true, makes the boundary-querying operation use an intersected part's BasePart.CanCollide value in favor of its BasePart.CanQuery value when determining whether that part is included in the array of spatial query results.

properties.name: BruteForceAllSlow
properties.documentation: Type: bool When enabled, the query will ignore all part collision properties and perform a brute-force check on every part. This will negatively impact performance and should not be used in live experiences.

properties.name: FilterDescendantsInstances
properties.documentation: Type: Array An array of objects whose descendants are used in filtering candidates. Note that this property has been superseded by ExcludeInstances and IncludeInstances which should be used for new work.

properties.name: FilterType
properties.documentation: Type: RaycastFilterType Determines whether the FilterDescendantsInstances array is used as an exclude or include list. Note that this property has been superseded by ExcludeInstances and IncludeInstances which should be used for new work.

methods.name: AddToFilter
methods.documentation: Adds the instances provided to FilterDescendantsInstances. Note that this property has been superseded by ExcludeInstances and IncludeInstances which should be used for new work.

dataTypes.name: Path2DControlPoint
dataTypes.documentation: Stores the info for a single control point used with the Path2D instance.

constructors.name: new
constructors.signature: Path2DControlPoint.new(Position: UDim2, Left Tangent: UDim2, Right Tangent: UDim2)
constructors.documentation: Returns a Path2DControlPoint with the position, left tangent, and right tangent set.

properties.name: Position
properties.documentation: Type: UDim2 The position of the Path2DControlPoint relative to the path's container.

properties.name: LeftTangent
properties.documentation: Type: UDim2 The left tangent of the Path2DControlPoint.

properties.name: RightTangent
properties.documentation: Type: UDim2 The right tangent of the Path2DControlPoint.

dataTypes.name: PathWaypoint
dataTypes.documentation: A description of the steps required to reach the next waypoint in a path.

constructors.name: new
constructors.signature: PathWaypoint.new(position: Vector3, action: PathWaypointAction, label: string)
constructors.documentation: Returns a PathWaypoint object from the given Vector3 position, PathWaypointAction action, and optional string label.

properties.name: Action
properties.documentation: Type: PathWaypointAction The action to perform at this waypoint as an PathWaypointAction.

properties.name: Position
properties.documentation: Type: Vector3 The 3D position of this waypoint.

properties.name: Label
properties.documentation: Type: string The name of the navigation area that generates this waypoint. Automatic jump links have Jump as their label.

dataTypes.name: PhysicalProperties
dataTypes.documentation: Describes properties that affect the physical behavior of a BasePart.

constructors.name: new
constructors.signature: PhysicalProperties.new(density: number, friction: number, elasticity: number, frictionWeight: number, elasticityWeight: number, acousticAbsorption: number)
constructors.documentation: Creates a PhysicalProperties container with the specified density, friction, elasticity, weight of friction, weight of elasticity, and acoustic absorption.

properties.name: AcousticAbsorption
properties.documentation: Type: number A value between 0 and 1 denoting how absorbent the material is to AudioEmitters. When using acoustic simulation, surfaces with higher absorption will result in less reverb than surfaces with lower absorption. Note that this does not affect the degree to which audio transmits through surfaces; for that, see Density.

properties.name: Density
properties.documentation: Type: number Density is defined as the amount of mass per unit volume. The more dense a part is, the more force it takes to accelerate it. Acceptable range is 0.0001 to 100.0 and values outside this range will be clamped. When using acoustic simulation, parts with higher density will muffle occluded AudioEmitters more.

properties.name: Friction
properties.documentation: Type: number Friction is defined as the force that opposes the relative lateral motion of two solid surfaces in contact. The greater the friction on a part, the quicker it will decelerate when it rubs against another part with friction. Acceptable range is 0.0 to 2.0 and values outside this range will be clamped.

properties.name: Elasticity
properties.documentation: Type: number Elasticity refers to a part's tendency to retain energy when colliding with another part. An Elasticity of 1 indicates that the part bounces with the same energy it had before a collision. Acceptable range is 0.0 to 1.0 and values outside this range will be clamped.

properties.name: FrictionWeight
properties.documentation: Type: number The friction weight of two parts rubbing together creates a ratio used to calculate the actual friction between the two parts. The higher a part's FrictionWeight, the more its Friction is used. Acceptable range is 0.0 to 100.0 and values outside this range will be clamped.

properties.name: ElasticityWeight
properties.documentation: Type: number The elasticity weight of two parts colliding creates a ratio used to calculate the actual elasticity between the two parts. The higher a part's ElasticityWeight, the more its Elasticity is used. Acceptable range is 0.0 to 100.0 and values outside this range will be clamped.

dataTypes.name: Random
dataTypes.documentation: Generates pseudorandom numbers and directions.

constructors.name: new
constructors.documentation: Returns a new Random object. If you don't provide the seed parameter, Random uses a seed from an internal entropy source. If you provide a seed, it should be within the range [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991], and Random will round it down to the nearest integer. So seeds of 0, 0.99, and math.random() all produce identical generators. If you need to generate a seed and store it for later retrieval, use math.random(max). Datatype.Random Generates a pseudorandom seed and uses it to create a new Random generator.

methods.name: NextInteger
methods.documentation: Returns a pseudorandom integer uniformly distributed over [min, max], inclusive of both endpoints. If min is greater than max, the two values are swapped so the call still succeeds. Both arguments are truncated toward zero to whole numbers before sampling.

methods.name: NextNumber
methods.documentation: Returns a uniform pseudorandom real number in the range of min to max, inclusive.

methods.name: Shuffle
methods.documentation: Uniformly shuffles the array part of tb in-place using NextInteger to pick indices. If there are any nil "holes" in the array part of the table, Shuffle throws an error, since shuffling could change the length. The hash part of tb is ignored. No metamethods of tb are invoked. The shuffle is defined to be a Fisher-Yates shuffle so the number of NextInteger calls is guaranteed to be consistent between engine versions for a given size of table.

methods.name: NextUnitVector
methods.documentation: Returns a unit vector with a pseudorandom direction. Vectors returned from this function are uniformly distributed over the unit sphere.

methods.name: Clone
methods.documentation: Returns a new Random object whose internal state is copied from the original. After cloning, both the original and the clone produce the same sequence of pseudorandom values going forward, but they advance independently — consuming a value from one does not affect the other.

dataTypes.name: Ray
dataTypes.documentation: Represents a line with a starting point that casts infinitely in a specific direction.

constructors.name: new
constructors.documentation: Returns a new Ray with given Origin and Direction.

properties.name: Unit
properties.documentation: Type: Ray The Ray with a normalized direction (the direction has a magnitude of 1).

properties.name: Origin
properties.documentation: Type: Vector3 The position of the origin.

properties.name: Direction
properties.documentation: Type: Vector3 The direction vector of the Ray.

methods.name: ClosestPoint
methods.documentation: Returns a Vector3 projected onto the ray so that it is within the Ray line of sight. Note: the Ray must be a unit ray for this method to behave as expected! the projection falls behind it.

methods.name: Distance
methods.documentation: Returns the distance between the given point and the point on the ray nearest to the given point (Ray.ClosestPoint(point)). the ray.

dataTypes.name: RaycastParams
dataTypes.documentation: A container for parameters used in raycasting operations.

constructors.name: new
constructors.documentation: Returns a blank RaycastParams object. Unlike other data type constructors, this constructor does not have any parameters, so you should set its properties appropriately.

properties.name: ExcludeInstances
properties.documentation: Type: {Instance}? An optional array of instances whose descendants will be excluded from the query. This property can be used simultaneously with IncludeInstances to allow for mixed filtering, for example including a large folder but excluding specific child instances. If an instance matches both an exclude and include filter, exclusions take priority over inclusions.

properties.name: IncludeInstances
properties.documentation: Type: {Instance}? An optional array of instances whose descendants will be included in the query. This property can be used simultaneously with ExcludeInstances to allow for mixed filtering. If an instance matches both an exclude and include filter, exclusions take priority over inclusions. Setting IncludeInstances to nil versus an empty array ({}) has opposite effects. IncludeInstances = nil is the most permissive filter (includes everything), whereas IncludeInstances = {} is the most restrictive filter (includes nothing).

properties.name: IgnoreWater
properties.documentation: Type: bool Determines whether the water material is considered when raycasting against Terrain.

properties.name: CollisionGroup
properties.documentation: Type: string Specifies a collision group for the raycasting operation. Parts in collision groups that are set to not collide with this group are ignored. If this property is omitted, the raycast assumes the Default collision group.

properties.name: RespectCanCollide
properties.documentation: Type: bool This property, if true, makes the raycast operation use an intersected part's CanCollide value in favor of its CanQuery value when determining whether that part is included in the RaycastResult.

properties.name: BruteForceAllSlow
properties.documentation: Type: bool When enabled, the query will ignore all part collision properties and perform a brute-force check on every part. This will negatively impact performance and should not be used in live experiences.

properties.name: Margin
properties.documentation: Type: number Expands the cast shape uniformly in every direction. Must be finite and greater than or equal to 0. Defaults to 0. Margin applies to WorldRoot:Shapecast(), WorldRoot:Blockcast(), WorldRoot:Spherecast() and WorldRoot:Raycast(). The expanded shape is what the maximum-size limit is checked against, so a large Margin can make an otherwise valid cast throw. Setting a non-zero Margin on a WorldRoot:Raycast() makes the operation behave as a sphere cast of that radius.

properties.name: SizeGradient
properties.documentation: Type: number Scales the cast shape over the length of the cast. Must be finite and greater than or equal to -1. Defaults to 0, which casts the shape at a constant size. The shape starts at its original size and is scaled by 1 + SizeGradient by the end of the cast, interpolating in between. A SizeGradient of 0.5 finishes the cast 50% larger, -0.5 finishes it at half size, and -1 shrinks it away entirely. SizeGradient scales the shape's own size, not Margin, so a cast with both keeps its margin at a constant width along the way. WorldRoot:Spherecast() is the exception: radius and margin are one and the same for a sphere, so both scale together.

properties.name: FilterDescendantsInstances
properties.documentation: Type: Array An array of objects whose descendants are used to filter raycasting candidates. Note that this property has been superseded by ExcludeInstances and IncludeInstances which should be used for new work.

properties.name: FilterType
properties.documentation: Type: RaycastFilterType Determines whether the FilterDescendantsInstances array is used as an exclude or include list. Note that this property has been superseded by ExcludeInstances and IncludeInstances which should be used for new work.

methods.name: AddToFilter
methods.documentation: Adds the instances provided to FilterDescendantsInstances. Note that this property has been superseded by ExcludeInstances and IncludeInstances which should be used for new work.

dataTypes.name: RaycastResult
dataTypes.documentation: Stores results from a raycast operation.

properties.name: Distance
properties.documentation: Type: number The distance between the ray origin and the intersection point.

properties.name: Instance
properties.documentation: Type: BasePart The BasePart or Terrain cell that the ray intersected.

properties.name: Material
properties.documentation: Type: Material The Material at the intersection point. For normal parts this is the BasePart.Material; for Terrain this can vary depending on terrain data.

properties.name: Position
properties.documentation: Type: Vector3 The world space point at which the intersection occurred, usually a point directly on the surface of the BasePart or Terrain cell.

properties.name: Normal
properties.documentation: Type: Vector3 The normal vector of the intersected face.

dataTypes.name: RBXScriptConnection
dataTypes.documentation: A connection between an RBXScriptSignal and a function.

properties.name: Connected
properties.documentation: Type: bool Describes whether or not the connection is still alive. This becomes false if Disconnect() is called.

methods.name: Disconnect
methods.documentation: Disconnects the connection from the event.

dataTypes.name: RBXScriptSignal
dataTypes.documentation: An object that runs connected functions upon a specific occurrence.

methods.name: Connect
methods.documentation: Establishes a function to be called when the event fires. Returns an RBXScriptConnection object associated with the connection. the event.

methods.name: ConnectParallel
methods.documentation: Establishes a function to be called when the event fires. Returns an RBXScriptConnection object associated with the connection. When the event fires, the signal callback is executed in a desynchronized state. Using ConnectParallel is similar to, but more efficient than, using Connect followed by a call to task.desynchronize() in the signal handler. Note: Scripts that connect in parallel must be rooted under an Actor. the event.

methods.name: Once
methods.documentation: Establishes a function to be called when the event fires. Returns an RBXScriptConnection object associated with the connection. The behavior of Once is similar to Connect. However, instead of allowing multiple events to be received by the specified function, only the first event will be delivered. Using Once also ensures that the connection to the function will be automatically disconnected prior the function being called. it fires.

methods.name: Wait
methods.documentation: Yields the current thread until the signal fires and returns the arguments provided by the signal.

dataTypes.name: Rect
dataTypes.documentation: A value that represents a two-dimensional rectangle.

constructors.name: new
constructors.signature: Rect.new(minX: number, minY: number, maxX: number, maxY: number)
constructors.documentation: Constructs a new Rect using minX and minY as coordinates for the top-left corner, and maxX and maxY as coordinates for the bottom-right corner.

properties.name: Width
properties.documentation: Type: number The horizontal span of the rectangle, equal to Max.X - Min.X. This value is always non-negative because the constructor normalizes the input coordinates so that Min is component-wise less than or equal to Max. Defaults to 0 for a Rect created with no arguments.

properties.name: Height
properties.documentation: Type: number The vertical span of the rectangle, equal to Max.Y - Min.Y. This value is always non-negative because the constructor normalizes the input coordinates so that Min is component-wise less than or equal to Max. Defaults to 0 for a Rect created with no arguments.

properties.name: Min
properties.documentation: Type: Vector2 The top-left corner of the rectangle as a Vector2. When you construct a Rect with two positions, this property returns the component-wise minimum of those positions regardless of the order they were passed in. Defaults to (0, 0) for a Rect created with no arguments.

properties.name: Max
properties.documentation: Type: Vector2 The bottom-right corner of the rectangle as a Vector2. When you construct a Rect with two positions, this property returns the component-wise maximum of those positions regardless of the order they were passed in. Defaults to (0, 0) for a Rect created with no arguments.

dataTypes.name: Region3
dataTypes.documentation: Describes a rectangular volume in 3D space.

constructors.name: new
constructors.documentation: Returns a new Region3 given the Vector3 bounds of the rectangular prism volume. Note that the order of the provided bounds matters: by switching them, the polarity of the size components will switch. It is possible to create a Region3 with a negative volume.

properties.name: CFrame
properties.documentation: Type: CFrame The CFrame representing the center position and orientation of the Region3. The position component is the midpoint of the min and max vectors passed to Region3.new(), computed as (min + max) / 2. Because a Region3 is always axis-aligned, the rotation component of the returned CFrame is always the identity (no rotation). This property is read-only.

properties.name: Size
properties.documentation: Type: Vector3 The size of the Region3 as a Vector3, equal to max - min from the constructor arguments. Individual components may be negative if the corresponding component of min is greater than max in the call to Region3.new(). This property is read-only.

methods.name: ExpandToGrid
methods.documentation: Expands the Region3 based on the provided resolution and returns the expanded Region3 aligned to the Terrain voxel grid. ceiled to the nearest multiple of resolution.

dataTypes.name: RotationCurveKey
dataTypes.documentation: A time-value pair used with RotationCurve instances.

constructors.name: new
constructors.signature: RotationCurveKey.new(time: number, cframe: CFrame, Interpolation: KeyInterpolationMode)
constructors.documentation: Creates a new RotationCurveKey at a given time with a given CFrame. LeftTangent and RightTangent are left uninitialized and, if not initialized, tangent values of 0 will be used when evaluating the curve.

properties.name: Interpolation
properties.documentation: Type: KeyInterpolationMode Defines the interpolation mode used for the curve segment that begins at this key and ends at the next key. Possible values are KeyInterpolationMode.Constant (holds the key's value until the next key), KeyInterpolationMode.Linear (linearly interpolates between this key and the next using spherical linear interpolation), and KeyInterpolationMode.Cubic (uses a cubic hermite spline shaped by RightTangent and the next key's LeftTangent). Defaults to KeyInterpolationMode.Cubic. Setting this property to a non-cubic mode automatically clears RightTangent (because tangent slope is only meaningful in cubic segments).

properties.name: Time
properties.documentation: Type: number The time position of this RotationCurveKey along the curve's timeline, in seconds. Keys within a RotationCurve are kept sorted by ascending time; inserting a key at the same time as an existing key replaces the existing key. Defaults to 0.

properties.name: Value
properties.documentation: Type: CFrame The rotation stored at this key, represented as a CFrame. Only the rotational component of the CFrame is used; the positional component is ignored. Defaults to CFrame.identity.

properties.name: RightTangent
properties.documentation: Type: number The outgoing tangent (slope) at this key, controlling the shape of the cubic segment that extends toward the next key. Defaults to 0. This property can only be set when Interpolation is KeyInterpolationMode.Cubic; attempting to set it on a key with a different interpolation mode raises a runtime error. Returns nil if the tangent has not been explicitly assigned.

properties.name: LeftTangent
properties.documentation: Type: number The incoming tangent (slope) at this key, controlling the shape of the cubic segment arriving from the previous key. Defaults to 0. Unlike RightTangent, this property can be set on a key regardless of its own interpolation mode, because the preceding segment may use cubic interpolation and needs a defined slope at its endpoint. Returns nil if the tangent has not been explicitly assigned.

dataTypes.name: SharedTable
dataTypes.documentation: Provides sharable, table-like storage for key/value pairs.

constructors.name: new
constructors.documentation: Returns a new SharedTable containing elements equivalent to those in the provided Luau table. If the provided Luau table contains any keys or values that cannot be stored in a SharedTable, construction of the SharedTable fails. See the summary at the top of this page for a list of types of objects that can be stored in a SharedTable. If the Luau table contains any table as a value, that table is converted into a new SharedTable. Note that in some cases it may be desirable to store a SharedTable in the SharedTableRegistry. The ShareTableRegistry:GetSharedTable() method provides a convenient way to accomplish this.

methods.name: clear
methods.documentation: Atomically removes all of the elements from a SharedTable. If the SharedTable is frozen, the operation fails and an error will be raised.

methods.name: clone
methods.documentation: Creates a clone of a SharedTable and returns the clone. If the optional deep argument is not present, or if it is present and its value is false, then a shallow clone is created. A shallow clone copies only the top-level SharedTable object. If any value in the SharedTable itself is a SharedTable, then both the original SharedTable and the clone SharedTable will refer to the same SharedTable. The shallow clone operation is atomic, so the clone SharedTable will contain a consistent snapshot of the state in the original SharedTable, even if it is being modified concurrently from other scripts. If the optional deep argument is present and its value is true, then a deep clone is created. A deep c

methods.name: cloneAndFreeze
methods.documentation: Creates a frozen (read-only) clone of a SharedTable and returns the clone. The behavior of this function is the same as the behavior of clone, except that the clone is frozen. If a deep clone is requested, then all of the cloned SharedTable objects are frozen.

methods.name: increment
methods.signature: SharedTable.increment(st: SharedTable, key: string | number, delta: number): number
methods.documentation: Atomically increments the value of an element. An element with the specified key must exist in the SharedTable, and it must be of type number. The specified delta is added to the value, and the original value is returned. The SharedTable.update function can also be used for this purpose; this increment function exists for convenience and performance (in general, increment is much faster than update, so it should be preferred where possible). The following two function calls have the same effect: If the SharedTable is frozen, the operation fails and an error will be raised. Increment Demonstrates usage of SharedTable.increment().

methods.name: isFrozen
methods.documentation: Returns true if the SharedTable is frozen (read-only).

methods.name: size
methods.documentation: Returns the number of elements stored in the SharedTable. Note that if other scripts are concurrently modifying the SharedTable, the returned size may no longer be correct after it is returned, since other scripts may have added or removed elements from the SharedTable.

methods.name: update
methods.signature: SharedTable.update(st: SharedTable, key: string | number, f: function): ()
methods.documentation: Atomically updates the value of an element. When a SharedTable is accessed concurrently from scripts running in different execution contexts, it is possible for their accesses to interleave unpredictably. Because of this, code like the following is generally incorrect, because the value may have changed between the read on the first line and the update on the second line: The update function makes it possible to perform an atomic update to an element. It takes a function that it will call with the current value of the element. The function can then compute and return the new value. Note that the function may be called multiple times if the SharedTable is being concurrently modified from othe

dataTypes.name: UDim
dataTypes.documentation: Represents a one-dimensional value with two components, a relative scale and an absolute offset.

constructors.name: new
constructors.documentation: Returns a new UDim from the given Scale and Offset components. Both parameters are optional and default to 0 when omitted; calling UDim.new() with no arguments produces a UDim equivalent to UDim.new(0, 0).

properties.name: Scale
properties.documentation: Type: number The relative scale component of the UDim, expressed as a fraction of a reference measurement (typically the corresponding axis of a parent GuiObject). A value of 1 represents the full reference measurement, 0.5 represents half, and 0 means the scale contributes nothing to the resolved pixel value. Defaults to 0 when not specified in the constructor. This property is read-only.

properties.name: Offset
properties.documentation: Type: number The absolute offset component of the UDim in pixels. This value is added to the resolved scale portion (Scale * referenceMeasurement) to produce the final pixel measurement. The offset is stored as an integer. Defaults to 0 when not specified in the constructor. This property is read-only.

constructors.name: fromId

constructors.name: fromString

User ToString For Storage Demonstrates User.ToString.

dataTypes.name: ValueCurveKey
dataTypes.documentation: A time-value pair used with ValueCurve instances.

constructors.name: new
constructors.signature: ValueCurveKey.new(time: number, value: any, Interpolation: KeyInterpolationMode)
constructors.documentation: Creates a new ValueCurveKey at a given time and value. LeftTangent and RightTangent are left uninitialized and, if not initialized, tangent values of '0' will be used when evaluating the curve.

properties.name: Interpolation
properties.documentation: Type: KeyInterpolationMode Specifies the interpolation mode used for the curve segment that begins at this key and ends at the next key on the ValueCurve. Each segment of the curve can use a different interpolation mode. The default value is KeyInterpolationMode.Constant. The available modes are: Not all value types support Linear or Cubic interpolation. Non-numerical types such as strings, booleans, and enums revert to Constant interpolation regardless of this setting. Changing this property to a non-cubic mode automatically clears the RightTangent of this key, because only cubic segments use a right tangent.

properties.name: Time
properties.documentation: Type: number The time position of this ValueCurveKey along the curve. Defaults to 0. Keys within a ValueCurve are stored sorted by their time values; the time determines where in the animation timeline this key's value applies.

properties.name: Value
properties.documentation: Type: any The value stored in this ValueCurveKey. Defaults to nil. Can hold any supported Luau type, including numbers, booleans, strings, Vector2, Vector3, CFrame, UDim, UDim2, NumberRange, NumberSequence, ColorSequence, and enums. All keys on a single ValueCurve must hold values of the same type; attempting to insert a key whose value type differs from existing keys produces an error.

properties.name: RightTangent
properties.documentation: Type: number The outgoing tangent (slope) at this key, used when the Interpolation is KeyInterpolationMode.Cubic. Defaults to nil (unset); when unset, an effective tangent of 0 is used during curve evaluation. Attempting to set this property on a key whose interpolation mode is not Cubic throws a runtime error. This property is automatically cleared when Interpolation is changed to a non-cubic mode.

properties.name: LeftTangent
properties.documentation: Type: number The incoming tangent (slope) at this key, used when the preceding segment uses KeyInterpolationMode.Cubic interpolation. Defaults to nil (unset); when unset, an effective tangent of 0 is used during curve evaluation. Unlike RightTangent, this property can be set on any key regardless of its own interpolation mode, because it defines the slope at the endpoint of the preceding cubic segment.

dataTypes.name: Vector2

constructors.name: new
constructors.documentation: Returns a Vector2 from the given x and y components. Both parameters default to 0 if not provided.

properties.name: X
properties.documentation: Type: number The x-coordinate of the Vector2, corresponding to the first argument passed to Vector2.new(). This property is read-only.

properties.name: Y
properties.documentation: Type: number The y-coordinate of the Vector2, corresponding to the second argument passed to Vector2.new(). This property is read-only.

properties.name: Magnitude
properties.documentation: Type: number The length (magnitude) of the Vector2, computed as math.sqrt(X^2 + Y^2). This property is read-only.

properties.name: Unit
properties.documentation: Type: Vector2 A normalized copy of the Vector2 — one that has the same direction as the original but a magnitude of 1. If the vector has zero magnitude the result is undefined (contains nan values). This property is read-only.

methods.name: Dot
methods.documentation: Returns the scalar dot product of this vector and v, computed as self.X * v.X + self.Y * v.Y. The result equals the product of the two magnitudes multiplied by the cosine of the angle between them. A positive value means the vectors point in roughly the same direction; zero means they are perpendicular; negative means they point in roughly opposite directions.

methods.name: Lerp
methods.documentation: Returns a Vector2 linearly interpolated between this Vector2 and the given goal v by the fraction alpha, using the formula self + (v - self) * alpha. An alpha of 0 returns self, an alpha of 1 returns v, and values between 0 and 1 return a point in between. Note that alpha is not clamped to [0, 1] — values outside that range extrapolate beyond the two endpoints.

methods.name: Cross
methods.documentation: Returns the 2D cross product of this vector with other, computed as self.X * other.Y - self.Y * other.X. Unlike Vector3:Cross() which returns a vector, the 2D cross product returns a scalar representing the signed magnitude of the perpendicular (Z) component. The result is positive when other is counter-clockwise from self, negative when clockwise, and zero when the vectors are parallel. as self.X * other.Y - self.Y * other.X.

methods.name: Abs
methods.documentation: Returns a new vector from the absolute values of the original's components. For example, a vector of (-2, 4) returns a vector of (2, 4). original's components.

methods.name: Ceil
methods.documentation: Returns a new vector from the ceiling of the original's components. For example, a vector of (-2.6, 5.1) returns a vector of (-2, 6). original's components.

methods.name: Floor
methods.documentation: Returns a new vector from the floor of the original's components. For example, a vector of (-2.6, 5.1) returns a vector of (-3, 5). original's components.

methods.name: Sign
methods.documentation: Returns a new vector from the sign (-1, 0, or 1) of the original's components. For example, a vector of (-2.6, 5.1) returns a vector of (-1, 1). original's components.

methods.name: Angle
methods.documentation: Returns the angle in radians between the two vectors. Specify true for the optional isSigned boolean if you want a signed angle. By default, the method returns the absolute value. Signed angles are a negative when going clockwise. Values are in the range [0, pi] for absolute angles and [-pi, pi] for signed angles.

methods.name: Max
methods.documentation: Returns a Vector2 with each component as the highest among the respective components of the provided Vector2 objects.

methods.name: Min
methods.documentation: Returns a Vector2 with each component as the lowest among the respective components of the provided Vector2 objects.

methods.name: FuzzyEq
methods.documentation: Returns true if the X and Y components of the other Vector2 are within epsilon units of each corresponding component of this Vector2. The comparison is per-component: both math.abs(self.X - other.X) and math.abs(self.Y - other.Y) must be less than or equal to epsilon. The optional epsilon parameter defaults to 1e-5 (0.00001) and must be a positive value no greater than 0.1.

dataTypes.documentation: Represents a 2D value with direction and magnitude.

constants.name: zero
constants.documentation: A Vector2 with a magnitude of zero.

constants.name: one
constants.documentation: A Vector2 with a value of 1 on every axis.

constants.name: xAxis

constants.name: yAxis

dataTypes.name: Vector2int16
dataTypes.documentation: Represents a Vector2 with signed 16-bit integers for components.

constructors.name: new
constructors.documentation: Returns a new Vector2int16 given the x and y components. Non-integer components are rounded down. The components must fall within the range [-2<sup>15</sup>, 2<sup>15</sup>). If outside this range, integer overflow may occur. For example, providing 32,768 (equal to 2<sup>15</sup>) as a component overflows the 16-bit integer, and so the component is -32,768 (equal to -2<sup>15</sup>) instead.

properties.name: X
properties.documentation: Type: number The x-coordinate of the Vector2int16, also accessible in its lower-case variant.

properties.name: Y
properties.documentation: Type: number The y-coordinate of the Vector2int16, also accessible in its lower-case variant.

dataTypes.name: Vector3

constructors.name: new
constructors.signature: Vector3.new(x: number?, y: number?, z: number?): Vector3
constructors.documentation: Returns a new Vector3 using the given x, y, and z components.

constructors.name: FromNormalId
constructors.documentation: Returns a unit Vector3 pointing in the direction of the given NormalId. For example, NormalId.Top returns (0, 1, 0) and NormalId.Front returns (0, 0, -1).

constructors.name: FromAxis
constructors.documentation: Returns a unit Vector3 for the given Axis. The mapping is Axis.X to (1, 0, 0), Axis.Y to (0, 1, 0), and Axis.Z to (0, 0, 1).

properties.name: X
properties.documentation: Type: number The X coordinate of the Vector3. In world space, this axis corresponds to the left-right (east-west) direction.

properties.name: Y
properties.documentation: Type: number The Y coordinate of the Vector3. In world space, this axis corresponds to the up-down (vertical) direction.

properties.name: Z
properties.documentation: Type: number The Z coordinate of the Vector3. In world space, this axis corresponds to the north-south (forward-back) direction.

properties.name: Magnitude
properties.documentation: Type: number The length (magnitude) of the Vector3, computed as math.sqrt(X^2 + Y^2 + Z^2). This is useful for comparing distances or determining how far a point is from the origin.

properties.name: Unit
properties.documentation: Type: Vector3 A normalized copy of the Vector3 — one that has the same direction as the original but a magnitude of 1. This is useful when you need only the direction of a vector without its length, for example to get a movement direction regardless of speed. If the vector has a magnitude of 0 (i.e. all components are zero), the resulting Unit vector will have NaN components. Check Magnitude before using Unit when the vector may be zero-length.

methods.name: Cross
methods.documentation: Returns the cross product of this vector and other. The resulting vector is perpendicular to both input vectors and has a magnitude equal to the area of the parallelogram they span. The direction follows the right-hand rule: if you curl the fingers of your right hand from self toward other, your thumb points in the direction of the result. The cross product is commonly used to find normals to surfaces, determine the axis of rotation between two directions, and test whether two vectors are parallel (cross product of parallel vectors is the zero vector).

methods.name: Dot
methods.documentation: Returns the scalar dot product of this vector and other, computed as self.X * other.X + self.Y * other.Y + self.Z * other.Z. The dot product is useful for determining the relationship between two directions: it equals the product of their magnitudes multiplied by the cosine of the angle between them. For unit vectors, a result of 1 means they point in the same direction, 0 means they are perpendicular, and -1 means they point in opposite directions.

methods.name: Lerp
methods.documentation: Returns a Vector3 linearly interpolated between this Vector3 and the given goal Vector3 by the fraction alpha. Note that alpha is not limited to the range [0, 1].

methods.name: Abs
methods.documentation: Returns a new vector from the absolute values of the original's components. For example, a vector of (-2, 4, -6) returns a vector of (2, 4, 6).

methods.name: Ceil
methods.documentation: Returns a new vector from the ceiling of the original's components. For example, a vector of (-2.6, 5.1, 8.8) returns a vector of (-2, 6, 9).

methods.name: Floor
methods.documentation: Returns a new vector from the floor of the original's components. For example, a vector of (-2.6, 5.1, 8.8) returns a vector of (-3, 5, 8).

methods.name: Sign
methods.documentation: Returns a new vector from the sign (-1, 0, or 1) of the original's components. For example, a vector of (-2.6, 5.1, 0) returns a vector of (-1, 1, 0).

methods.name: Angle
methods.documentation: Returns the angle in radians between this vector and other. The input vectors do not need to be unit vectors. Without an axis argument, the returned angle is always in the range [0, math.pi] (unsigned). If you provide an axis Vector3, the returned angle is signed: positive when the rotation from self to other follows the right-hand rule around axis, and negative otherwise. The signed result is in the range [-math.pi, math.pi]. The axis is used only to determine the sign; the plane of rotation is still defined by self and other.

methods.name: FuzzyEq
methods.documentation: Returns true if the two vectors are approximately equal within the tolerance defined by epsilon. The comparison is performed per-component using a hybrid epsilon that scales relative to the magnitude of each component, making it suitable for both small and large values. The default epsilon of 0.00001 (1e-5) works well for most cases.

methods.name: Max
methods.documentation: Returns a Vector3 with each component as the highest among the respective components of both provided Vector3 objects.

methods.name: Min
methods.documentation: Returns a Vector3 with each component as the lowest among the respective components of both provided Vector3 objects.

constants.documentation: A Vector3 with a magnitude of 0.

constants.documentation: A Vector3 with a value of 1 on every axis.

constants.documentation: A Vector3 with a value of 1 on the X axis.

constants.name: yAxis
constants.documentation: A Vector3 with a value of 1 on the Y axis.

constants.documentation: A Vector3 with a value of 1 on the Z axis.
