events.signature: UserInputService.TouchDrag(dragDirection: SwipeDirection, numberOfTouches: int, gameProcessedEvent: boolean)
events.documentation: This event fires when the user drags on the screen of a TouchEnabled device. Use this event to detect the start of a deliberate directional gesture (for example, sliding an element left or right to reveal contextual actions) before the user commits to a direction; for detecting a completed swipe or fling gesture, use TouchSwipe instead. Note that this event only fires when the Roblox client window is in focus. It will not fire when the window is minimized. *Security: None · Capabilities: Input*

events.name: TouchEnded
events.documentation: This event fires when a user releases their finger from the screen of a TouchEnabled device. Can be paired with TouchStarted to determine when a user starts and stops touching the screen. Note that this event only fires when the Roblox client window is in focus. It will not fire when the window is minimized. *Security: None · Capabilities: Input*

events.name: TouchLongPress
events.documentation: This event fires when a user holds at least one finger for a short amount of time on the screen of a TouchEnabled device. Note that this event only fires when the Roblox client window is in focus. It will not fire when the window is minimized. *Security: None · Capabilities: Input*

events.name: TouchMoved
events.documentation: This event fires when a user moves their finger on the screen of a TouchEnabled device, useful for tracking whether a user is moving their finger on the screen and where they're moving it. Can be paired with TouchStarted and TouchEnded to determine when a user starts touching the screen, how their finger moves while touching it, and when the they stop touching the screen. Note that this event only fires when the Roblox client window is in focus. It will not fire when the window is minimized. *Security: None · Capabilities: Input*

events.name: TouchPan
events.signature: UserInputService.TouchPan(touchPositions: Array, totalTranslation: Vector2, velocity: Vector2, state: UserInputState, gameProcessedEvent: boolean)
events.documentation: This event fires when the user drags at least one finger on the screen of a TouchEnabled device. Note that this event only fires when the Roblox client window is in focus. It will not fire when the window is minimized. *Security: None · Capabilities: Input*

events.name: TouchPinch
events.signature: UserInputService.TouchPinch(touchPositions: Array, scale: float, velocity: float, state: UserInputState, gameProcessedEvent: boolean)
events.documentation: This event fires when a user performs a pinch gesture on the screen of a TouchEnabled device. Note that this event only fires when the Roblox client window is in focus. It will not fire when the window is minimized. *Security: None · Capabilities: Input*

events.name: TouchRotate
events.signature: UserInputService.TouchRotate(touchPositions: Array, rotation: float, velocity: float, state: UserInputState, gameProcessedEvent: boolean)
events.documentation: This event fires when a user rotates two fingers on the screen of a TouchEnabled device. Note that this event only fires when the Roblox client window is in focus. It will not fire when the window is minimized. *Security: None · Capabilities: Input*

events.name: TouchStarted
events.documentation: This event fires when a user places their finger on the screen of a TouchEnabled device. Can be paired with TouchEnded to determine when a user starts and stops touching the screen. Note that this event only fires when the Roblox client window is in focus. It will not fire when the window is minimized. *Security: None · Capabilities: Input*

events.name: TouchSwipe
events.documentation: This event fires on a TouchEnabled device when a user places their finger(s) down on the screen, pans across the screen, and lifts their finger(s) off with a certain speed of movement. For more precise tracking of touch input movement, use TouchMoved. Note that this event only fires when the Roblox client window is in focus. It will not fire when the window is minimized. *Security: None · Capabilities: Input*

events.name: TouchTap
events.documentation: This event fires when a user taps their finger on the screen of a TouchEnabled device, regardless of whether the user taps in the 3D world or on a GuiObject element. If you're looking for an event that only fires when the user taps in the 3D world, use TouchTapInWorld. Note that this event only fires when the Roblox client window is in focus. It will not fire when the window is minimized. *Security: None · Capabilities: Input*

events.name: TouchTapInWorld
events.documentation: This event fires when a user taps their finger on the screen of a TouchEnabled device and the tap location is in the 3D world rather than on a GuiObject element. Note that this event only fires when the Roblox client window is in focus. It will not fire when the window is minimized. *Security: None · Capabilities: Input*

events.name: WindowFocused
events.documentation: This event fires when the window of the Roblox client gains focus, typically when it is maximized or actively opened by the user. Can be used alongside WindowFocusReleased to track when the client loses focus on a user's screen. *Security: None · Capabilities: Input*

events.name: WindowFocusReleased
events.documentation: This event fires when the window of the Roblox client loses focus, typically when it is minimized by the user. Can be used alongside WindowFocused to track when the client gains focus on a user's screen. *Security: None · Capabilities: Input* Window Focus Away Script (LocalScript) The purpose of this code sample is to fire a server-side RemoteEvent to indicate when the player is "away" based on their client window being minimized. When mimimized, the server creates a ForceField around the player's character to shield them from damage. The code below should be placed in a LocalScript within StarterPlayerScripts with the intention of running it in conjunction with the server-side Script that f

events.name: UserCFrameChanged
events.documentation: Deprecated: Use VRService.UserCFrameChanged instead. The UserCFrameChanged event fires when the CFrame of a VR device changes. This event can be used to track the movement of a connected VR device. Using the event, you can implement features such as moving the user's in-game character limbs as the user moves their VR device. This can be done by changing the CFrame of the user's in-game limbs to match the CFrame changes of the VR device using the UserCFrame enum and _CFrame_ value arguments passed by the event. To retrieve the CFrame of a connected VR device, use UserInputService:GetUserCFrame().

classes.name: UserService
classes.documentation: A service that handles queries regarding users on the Roblox platform.

methods.name: GetUserInfosByUserIdsAsync
methods.documentation: This function lets you request information about users outside of the current DataModel in bulk. The input and output values are both arrays. The signature of a singular user info object is: *Yields · Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Basic* UserService:GetUserInfosByUserIdsAsync Example Expected output: Id: 156 Username: builderman DisplayName: builderman Id: 1 Username: Roblox DisplayName: Roblox Id: 735878936 Username: Cozecant DisplayName: cozecant

methods.name: GetUserFromGlobalUserIdAsync
methods.documentation: Resolves a global user ID to a User for the current experience domain. Use this when you have a legacy global user ID (for example, one previously saved in a data store) and need the corresponding User value. This is a server-only yielding call. *Yields · Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Basic* identity. Get User From Global User Id Async Demonstrates UserService:GetUserFromGlobalUserIdAsync().

classes.name: UserSettings
classes.documentation: A singleton object that houses basic user settings, which persist across all games on Roblox.

methods.name: IsUserFeatureEnabled
methods.documentation: Returns true if the specified user feature is enabled. This will throw an error if the user feature does not exist. This function checks user features whose names start with "User". It is intended for Roblox-created scripts. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Players* false. IsUserFeatureEnabled Sample A basic sample of how the IsUserFeatureEnabled function is used by Roblox to control certain features.

methods.name: Reset
methods.documentation: Erases the saved state of the UserSettings, and restores its values back to default. This function will fail to run correctly from a LocalScript, as it does not have permission to restore all of the properties in the UserGameSettings class. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Players*

classes.name: ValueBase
classes.documentation: Base class of all \"value instance\" objects.

classes.name: ValueCurve
classes.documentation: A sorted list of time-value pairs that define a curve. Used to animate any type of value.

properties.name: Length
properties.documentation: Number of keys in the value curve.

properties.name: ValueType
properties.documentation: Read-only value indicating the type held in this curve, or the string "Nil" if there are no keys.

methods.name: GetKeyAtIndex
methods.documentation: Returns a copy of a key at a given index. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Basic*

methods.name: GetKeyIndicesAtTime
methods.documentation: The first item in the returned array is the index of the last key with time less than or equal to time (or the lesser of either 1 or the curve length if no key was found). The second item in the returned array is the index of the first key with time greater than or equal to time (or the curve length if no key was found satisfying the inequality). *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Basic* at or before time, and the index of the first key at or after time.

methods.name: GetKeys
methods.documentation: Returns a copy of all the keys in the ValueCurve as a Luau array of ValueCurveKeys. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Basic*

methods.name: GetValueAtTime
methods.documentation: Samples the value curve at a given time passed as argument. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Basic*

methods.name: InsertKey
methods.documentation: Adds the key passed as an argument to this curve. If a key at the same time is found, it will be replaced. In the returned array, the first value is true if a key was added or false if a previous key was replaced; the second value is the index at which the marker was added. If there are not yet any keys, then the key may be added. If keys exist, the type of the value must match those of existing keys; otherwise a message is printed and {false, -1} is returned. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Basic*

methods.name: InsertKeyValue
methods.signature: ValueCurve:InsertKeyValue(time: float, value: Variant, Interpolation: KeyInterpolationMode): Array
methods.documentation: Creates a ValueCurveKey from the given arguments and inserts it in this curve. If a key at the same time is found, it will be replaced. In the returned array, the first value is true if a key was added or false if a previous key was replaced; the second value is the index at which the marker was added. If there are not yet any keys, then the key may be added. If keys exist, the type of the value must match those of existing keys; otherwise a message is printed and {false, -1} is returned. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Basic*

methods.name: RemoveKeyAtIndex
methods.documentation: Removes a given number (count) of keys starting from the startingIndex index and returns the number of keys that were removed. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Basic*

methods.name: SetKeys
methods.documentation: Resets this curve's keys using the ValueCurveKey array passed as an argument. Keys in the keys array are sorted in ascending time order before insertion, and keys at duplicated times are removed in a stable manner. Returns the number of keys actually inserted. Keys previously stored in this curve are removed before the keys passed as arguments are added. The keys must all contain values of the same type. And that type must match any existing keys. Otherwise a message is printed, the keys are not added, and 0 is returned. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Basic*

classes.name: Vector3Curve
classes.documentation: Represents a 3D vector curve, grouping three FloatCurve instances.

methods.name: GetValueAtTime
methods.documentation: Returns the three FloatCurves (X, Y, Z) at the passed time argument as an array of three numbers. If a channel curve is missing or no key is found in the curve, the channel is evaluated as nil. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Basic* argument.

methods.name: X
methods.documentation: Returns the FloatCurve controlling the X channel (the first child instance of type FloatCurve named X). If none is found, an empty FloatCurve is created. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Basic* empty FloatCurve if none exists yet.

methods.name: Y
methods.documentation: Returns the FloatCurve controlling the Y channel (the first child instance of type FloatCurve named Y). If none is found, an empty FloatCurve is created. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Basic* empty FloatCurve if none exists yet.

methods.name: Z
methods.documentation: Returns the FloatCurve controlling the Z channel (the first child instance of type FloatCurve named Z). If none is found, an empty FloatCurve is created. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Basic* empty FloatCurve if none exists yet.

classes.name: Vector3Value
classes.documentation: A container object for a single Vector3 value.

properties.name: Value
properties.documentation: The stored Vector3.

events.name: Changed
events.documentation: Fired whenever the Vector3Value.Value of the Vector3Value is changed. It will run with the new value being stored in the argument object, instead of a string representing the property being changed. This event, like other changed events, can be used to track when an Vector3Value changes and to track the different values that it may change to. For instance, this may be useful in games that rely on Vector3Values to track positions in the game world. Equivalent changed events exist for similar objects, such as NumberValue and StringValue, depending on what object type best suits the need. *Security: None*

events.name: changed
events.documentation: Deprecated: This deprecated event is a variant of Vector3Value.Changed which should be used instead. *Security: None*

classes.name: VectorForce
classes.documentation: Applies constant force to an assembly.

properties.name: ApplyAtCenterOfMass
properties.documentation: When true, force is applied at the center of mass of the parent assembly of Attachment0. When false, force is applied at Attachment0.

properties.name: Force
properties.documentation: The strength and direction of the force.

properties.name: RelativeTo
properties.documentation: This property determines the CFrame in which the force is expressed.

classes.name: VehicleController
classes.documentation: An object responsible for translating a seated player's directional input into throttle and steering for a VehicleSeat.

classes.name: VehicleSeat
classes.documentation: A seat object that can be used to control a vehicle.

properties.name: AreHingesDetected
properties.documentation: Displays how many hinges are detected by the VehicleSeat. Useful for debugging vehicle designs.

properties.name: Disabled
properties.documentation: Toggles whether the VehicleSeat is active or not. If the seat is disabled, it will not automatically weld a character to it on collision and will not allow a character to control the connected vehicle.

properties.name: HeadsUpDisplay
properties.documentation: If true, a UI speed bar will be displayed on screen that tells you what speed the vehicle is moving at.

properties.name: MaxSpeed
properties.documentation: The maximum speed that can be attained.

properties.name: Occupant
properties.documentation: The Humanoid that is sitting in the seat.

properties.name: Steer
properties.documentation: The direction of movement, tied to left and right movement inputs. Can be either 1 (right), 0 (straight), or -1 (left). Will refresh back to 0 unless constantly set.

properties.name: SteerFloat
properties.documentation: The left-to-right movement float, tied to left and right movement inputs. Can range between 1 (right) and -1 (left). Will refresh back to 0 (straight) unless constantly set.

properties.name: Throttle
properties.documentation: The direction of throttle, tied to forward and backward movement inputs. Can be either 1 (forward), 0 (null), or -1 (reverse). Will refresh back to 0 unless constantly set.

properties.name: ThrottleFloat
properties.documentation: The forward-to-reverse throttle float, tied to forward and backward movement inputs. Can range between 1 (forward) and -1 (reverse). Will refresh back to 0 (null) unless constantly set.

properties.name: Torque
properties.documentation: How fast the vehicle will be able to attain MaxSpeed. The greater the number, the faster it will reach the maximum speed.

properties.name: TurnSpeed
properties.documentation: The speed at which the vehicle will turn. Higher numbers can cause problems and are not necessarily better.

methods.name: Sit
methods.documentation: Forces the character with the specified Humanoid to sit in the VehicleSeat. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Basic, AvatarBehavior*

classes.name: VelocityMotor
classes.documentation: A Motor-like JointInstance that forms its connection using a MotorFeature and a Hole.

properties.name: CurrentAngle
properties.documentation: Displays the angle that the motor is at in radians.

properties.name: DesiredAngle
properties.documentation: The desired angle to be reached. The motor will attempt to reach this angle.

properties.name: Hole
properties.documentation: The Hole linked to this VelocityMotor.

properties.name: MaxVelocity
properties.documentation: The maximum amount of velocity able to be reached.

classes.name: VideoCapture
classes.documentation: A child class of Capture for videos.

properties.name: FilePath
properties.documentation: Requires RobloxScript security; experience scripts cannot read it even when they hold the VideoCapture object. Absolute path on the user's device to the video file this capture represents: the temporary file while recording is in progress, or, after PromptSaveCapturesToGallery(), the permanent gallery location. Defaults to an empty string until a recording has produced a video file.

properties.name: TimeLength
properties.documentation: Duration of the video capture, in seconds. Populated once recording finishes, whether via StopVideoCapture() or because the capture's time limit was reached. Defaults to 0 until recording has finished.

classes.name: VideoCaptureService
classes.documentation: Service that manages camera capture for features such as avatar facial-animation tracking. Requires RobloxScript security; not callable from experience scripts.

classes.name: VideoDisplay
classes.documentation: A GUI object that displays video content from a connected VideoPlayer.

properties.name: ResampleMode
properties.documentation: Determines how the video looks when it is scaled. By default, the video smooths out texturing when displayed on the screen larger or smaller than its size in texture memory. When set to Enum.ResamplerMode.Pixelated, the video preserves the sharp edges of pixels.

properties.name: ScaleType
properties.documentation: Determines how a video texture is rendered when the UI element's aspect ratio differs from the source video's aspect ratio. By default, this property is ScaleType.Stretch which will simply stretch/compact the video texture dimensions so it fits the UI element's space exactly.

properties.name: TileSize
properties.documentation: This property sets the tiling size of the VideoDisplay with a default of <Typography noWrap>UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0)</Typography>. Tiling starts at the top-left corner of the video. This property is only active if the ScaleType for the VideoDisplay is set to ScaleType.Tile.

properties.name: VideoColor3
properties.documentation: Determines how a video is colorized. When set to white, no colorization occurs. This property is useful for reusing video assets.

properties.name: VideoRectOffset
properties.documentation: Allows the partial display of a video in conjunction with VideoRectSize. This property determines the pixel offset (from the top-left) of the video area to be displayed.

properties.name: VideoRectSize
properties.documentation: Allows the partial display of a video in conjunction with VideoRectOffset. This property determines the pixel size of the video area to be displayed. If either dimension is set to 0, the entire video is displayed instead.

properties.name: VideoTransparency
properties.documentation: Determines the alpha of a UI element's rendered video texture. A value of 0 is completely opaque, and a value of 1 is completely transparent (invisible).

methods.name: GetConnectedWires
methods.documentation: Returns an array of Wires that are connected to the specified pin. VideoDisplay has one "Input" pin. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: UI*

methods.name: GetInputPins
methods.documentation: Gets the list of pins that Wire can use in Wire.TargetName to connect to this instance via its Wire.TargetInstance property. For VideoDisplay, this is Input only. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: UI*

methods.name: GetOutputPins
methods.documentation: Gets the list of pins that Wire can use in Wire.SourceName to connect to this instance via its Wire.SourceInstance property. For VideoDisplay, there are none. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: UI*

events.name: WiringChanged
events.signature: VideoDisplay.WiringChanged(connected: boolean, pin: string, wire: Wire, instance: Instance)
events.documentation: Fires after a Wire becomes connected or disconnected, and that Wire is now or was previously connected to a pin on the VideoDisplay and to some other wirable instance. *Security: None · Capabilities: UI*

classes.name: VideoFrame
classes.documentation: A GUI object that renders a rectangle, like a Frame does, with a moving video image.

properties.name: IsLoaded
properties.documentation: This property will be true when the VideoFrame.Video has loaded from Roblox servers and is ready to play.

properties.name: Looped
properties.documentation: This property sets whether or not the VideoFrame.Video repeats once it has finished when it is playing.

properties.name: Playing
properties.documentation: This property indicates whether the VideoFrame.Video is currently playing. It can be set to start or pause playback as an alternative to the VideoFrame:Play() and VideoFrame:Pause() functions.

properties.name: Resolution
properties.documentation: This property gets the original source resolution of the VideoFrame.Video file.

properties.name: RollOffMaxDistance
properties.documentation: The maximum distance, in studs, a client's listener can be from the VideoFrame's part and still hear its audio. Defaults to 10000. This property only affects playback when the VideoFrame is 3D, as described in the class's "2D and 3D Sound" section; it has no effect on a global VideoFrame. How RollOffMaxDistance affects the attenuation of the sound depends on the RollOffMode property.

properties.name: RollOffMinDistance
properties.documentation: The minimum distance, in studs, at which the VideoFrame's audio begins to attenuate (decrease in volume). Defaults to 1. This property only affects playback when the VideoFrame is 3D, as described in the class's "2D and 3D Sound" section; it has no effect on a global VideoFrame. How RollOffMinDistance affects the attenuation of the sound depends on the RollOffMode property.

properties.name: RollOffMode
properties.documentation: Controls how the volume of the VideoFrame's audio attenuates (fades out) as the distance between the listener and the video's part changes. Defaults to RollOffMode.Inverse. This property only affects playback when the VideoFrame is 3D, as described in the class's "2D and 3D Sound" section; it has no effect on a global VideoFrame. For details on the different modes, see RollOffMode.

properties.name: TimeLength
properties.documentation: This property indicates the length of the VideoFrame.Video in seconds. If the video is not loaded, this value will be 0.

properties.name: TimePosition
properties.documentation: This property indicates the progress in seconds of the VideoFrame.Video. It can be changed to move the playback position of the video both before and during playback.

properties.name: Video
properties.documentation: The content ID of the video file a VideoFrame object is associated with. To save resources and improve performance, set this property to "" when the VideoFrame is not visible or in use. Creating and Playing a Video The code sample below demonstrates how to create and play a VideoFrame with some valid asset ID after the video has loaded.

properties.name: VideoContent
properties.documentation: The video content a VideoFrame object is associated with. Setting this property is equivalent to setting Video, and reading it returns a content ID equal to Video. When referencing a video by content ID, build the value with the corresponding Content constructor: Content.fromAssetId() for a numeric asset ID, or Content.fromUri() for an rbxassetid:// URI. Unlike Video, which only accepts a content ID string, VideoContent can also hold a direct reference to a VideoCapture object, such as one retrieved through CaptureService:ReadCapturesFromGalleryAsync(). This lets a local screen recording play back on the VideoFrame without first uploading it to Roblox. Build the value with Content.fromObject

properties.name: Volume
properties.documentation: This property determines how loud the VideoFrame.Video plays back. It can be set to a number between 0 and 100.

properties.name: MaximumResolution
properties.documentation: Internal-only. Caps the resolution the video is allowed to stream at, as an VideoSampleSize rather than exact pixel dimensions. The video may still stream below the cap on a slow connection. Defaults to VideoSampleSize.Full.

methods.name: Pause
methods.documentation: Sets VideoFrame.Playing to false, pausing playback if the VideoFrame.Video is playing. As VideoFrame.TimePosition is not reset, when the video is resumed it will continue from its previous position. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Audio, UI*

methods.name: Play
methods.documentation: Sets VideoFrame.Playing to true, playing the VideoFrame.Video from the current VideoFrame.TimePosition. To save resources and improve performance, set the VideoFrame.Video property to "" when the VideoFrame is not visible or in use. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Audio, UI* Creating and Playing a Video The code sample below demonstrates how to create and play a VideoFrame with some valid asset ID after the video has loaded.

events.name: DidLoop
events.documentation: An event that fires whenever the VideoFrame.Video loops. Returns the content ID of the video. *Security: None · Capabilities: Audio, UI*

events.name: Ended
events.documentation: This event fires when the VideoFrame.Video has completed playback and stopped. *Security: None · Capabilities: Audio, UI*

events.name: Loaded
events.documentation: This event fires when the VideoFrame.Video is loaded. *Security: None · Capabilities: Audio, UI*

events.name: Paused
events.documentation: This event fires whenever the VideoFrame.Video is paused using VideoFrame:Pause() or by setting VideoFrame.Playing to false. *Security: None · Capabilities: Audio, UI*

events.name: Played
events.documentation: This event fires whenever the VideoFrame.Video is played using the VideoFrame:Play() function or by setting VideoFrame.Playing to true. *Security: None · Capabilities: Audio, UI*

classes.name: VideoPlayer
classes.documentation: Used to play video assets.

properties.name: AutoLoadInStudio
properties.documentation: By default, VideoContent does not load while in Studio Edit mode and shows no output when wired to VideoDisplay to reduce studio memory usage. Toggle this option to load VideoContent while in Studio Edit mode.

properties.name: AutoPlayInStudio
properties.documentation: Plays the VideoContent while in Studio Edit mode. AutoLoadInStudio must be on for this option to show.

properties.name: IsLoaded
properties.documentation: This property is true when the VideoContent has loaded and is ready to play.

properties.name: IsPlaying
properties.documentation: Denotes whether this VideoPlayer is currently playing. This property is read-only, but replicates. To play and pause a VideoPlayer at runtime, use the Play() and Pause() methods.

properties.name: Looping
properties.documentation: Controls whether this VideoPlayer loops after reaching the end of its TimeLength.

properties.name: PlaybackSpeed
properties.documentation: Multiplier that controls how quickly the video plays, directly controlling the perceived pitch of the audio track. Ranges from 0 to 1.

properties.name: Resolution
properties.documentation: This property gets the original source resolution of the VideoContent file.

properties.name: TimeLength
properties.documentation: This property indicates the length of the VideoContent in seconds. If the video is not loaded, this value is 0.

properties.name: TimePosition
properties.documentation: This property indicates the progress in seconds of the VideoContent. It can be changed to move the playback position of the video both before and during playback.

properties.name: VideoContent
properties.documentation: The content ID of the video file a VideoPlayer object is associated with. To save resources and improve performance, call the Unload() method to unload the VideoContent when the VideoPlayer is not visible or in use.

properties.name: Volume
properties.documentation: Volume level, which is multiplied onto the output audio stream, controlling how loudly the audio track plays. Ranges from 0 to 3.

properties.name: MaximumResolution
properties.documentation: The maximum resolution, as an VideoSampleSize value, that the video decoder produces when playing this VideoPlayer. Defaults to VideoSampleSize.Full, which doesn't limit the decoded resolution. Lower VideoSampleSize values reduce the resolution the decoder outputs, which can lower memory usage on constrained devices.

methods.name: GetConnectedWires
methods.documentation: Returns an array of Wires that are connected to the specified pin. VideoPlayer has one "Output" pin. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Audio, UI*

methods.name: GetInputPins
methods.documentation: Gets the list of pins that Wire can use in Wire.TargetName to connect to this instance via its Wire.TargetInstance property. For VideoPlayer, there are none. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Audio, UI*

methods.name: GetOutputPins
methods.documentation: Gets the list of pins that Wire can use in Wire.SourceName to connect to this instance via its Wire.SourceInstance property. For VideoPlayer, this is Output only. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Audio, UI*

methods.name: LoadAsync
methods.documentation: VideoContent is typically only loaded when Play() is called, causing some buffering delay. This function can preload VideoContent so that it can be immediately played when Play() is called. Loading videos can consume a significant amount of device memory. *Yields · Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Audio, UI* AssetFetchStatus.Success once the VideoContent has loaded, or a failure status such as AssetFetchStatus.Failure or AssetFetchStatus.TimedOut if it could not be fetched.

methods.name: Pause
methods.documentation: Pauses the VideoPlayer wherever its TimePosition is. Replicates from server to client. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Audio, UI*

methods.name: Play
methods.documentation: Plays the VideoPlayer from wherever its TimePosition is. Replicates from server to client. To save resources and improve performance, call the Unload() method to unload the VideoContent when the VideoPlayer is not visible or in use. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Audio, UI*

methods.name: Unload
methods.documentation: Unloads the VideoContent to save resources. After calling this method, the IsLoaded property is false, and the TimePosition resets to 0. To play the video again, the LoadAsync() or Play() method must be called to reload the video. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Audio, UI*

events.name: DidEnd
events.documentation: Fires after the VideoPlayer has completed playback and stopped. Note this event does not fire for videos with Looped set to true since it continues playing upon reaching its end. This event also does not fire when the video is stopped before playback has completed; for this, use VideoPlayer:GetPropertyChangedSignal() on the IsPlaying property. *Security: None · Capabilities: Audio, UI*

events.name: DidLoop
events.documentation: Event that fires after the VideoPlayer loops. This happens when the video reaches the end of its content. This event does not fire if the video is looped manually by changing its TimePosition. *Security: None · Capabilities: Audio, UI*

events.name: PlayFailed
events.documentation: Fires when the VideoPlayer fails to load or play its VideoContent. The error parameter is an AssetFetchStatus value that describes why the content couldn't be fetched. *Security: None · Capabilities: Audio, UI*

events.name: WiringChanged
events.signature: VideoPlayer.WiringChanged(connected: boolean, pin: string, wire: Wire, instance: Instance)
events.documentation: Event that fires after a Wire becomes connected or disconnected, and that Wire is now or was previously connected to a pin on the VideoPlayer and to some other wirable instance. *Security: None · Capabilities: Audio, UI*

classes.name: VideoSampler
classes.documentation: An object for sampling frames from video content.

properties.name: TimeLength
properties.documentation: The length of the VideoContent in seconds.

properties.name: VideoContent
properties.documentation: The asset loaded into the VideoSampler.

methods.name: GetSamplesAtTimesAsync
methods.documentation: This method allows you to get a set of image frames from a video at specified timestamps as image Content objects. *Yields · Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: UI* a requested timestamp is out of range or the VideoSampler was unable to produce a sample, the corresponding entry in the returned array will be nil. Each dictionary contains the following keys:

classes.name: VideoService
classes.documentation: An internal service that offers no functionality to developers.

methods.name: CreateVideoSamplerAsync
methods.documentation: Creates a VideoSampler that samples frames from the provided video content. *Yields · Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: UI*

classes.name: ViewportFrame
classes.documentation: GuiObject that renders 3D objects inside its bounds.

properties.name: Ambient
properties.documentation: This property determines the lighting hue applied to the area within the ViewportFrame. Defaults to <Typography noWrap>Color3.fromRGB(200, 200, 200)</Typography> (ghost grey).

properties.name: CurrentCamera
properties.documentation: Camera instance that is used to render children objects. Defaults to nil. The Camera object does not replicate so the ViewportFrame.CurrentCamera won't replicate either. When you set this property, Camera.CFrame and Camera.FieldOfView will be saved and replicate with the ViewportFrame internally so the client can render the frame without a Camera object.

properties.name: ImageColor3
properties.documentation: This property determines how the rendered viewport image will be colorized, allowing you to change the color without directly modifying the rendered object. The default colorization value is <Typography noWrap>Color3.new(1, 1, 1)</Typography> (white) at which no color modification occurs. See also ImageTransparency which determines the transparency of the rendered image.

properties.name: ImageTransparency
properties.documentation: This property determines the transparency of the rendered viewport image, allowing you to change the transparency without directly modifying the rendered object. A value of 0 (default) is completely opaque and a value of 1 is completely transparent (invisible). See also ImageColor3 which determines how the rendered image will be colorized.

properties.name: LightColor
properties.documentation: The color of the emitted light. Defaults to <Typography noWrap>Color3.fromRGB(140, 140, 140)</Typography> (silver).

properties.name: LightDirection
properties.documentation: A Vector3 representing the direction of the light source from position <Typography noWrap>(0, 0, 0)</Typography>. Defaults to <Typography noWrap>Vector3.new(-1, -1, -1)</Typography>.

classes.name: VirtualInput
classes.documentation: Simulates mouse, keyboard, and pointer input as if it were performed by a real player.

methods.name: SendKey
methods.signature: VirtualInput:SendKey(isPressed: boolean, keyCode: KeyCode, isRepeatedKey?: boolean): ()
methods.documentation: This method injects a keyboard key press or release event, processed identically to a real hardware key event. This method throws a runtime error if CoreGui has keyboard focus, which includes a TextBox inside CoreGui being focused, a CoreGui element selected for keyboard or gamepad navigation, or the in-game escape menu being open. It also throws if the requested key is permanently bound to a Roblox core action (for example, the <kbd>Escape</kbd> key). Set isRepeatedKey to true only when simulating the OS auto-repeat behavior that occurs while a player physically holds a key down which fires a stream of repeated events after the initial key press. This is meaningful only for text-manipulatio

methods.name: SendMouseButton
methods.signature: VirtualInput:SendMouseButton(position: Vector2, button: UserInputType, isDown: boolean, repeatCount?: int): ()
methods.documentation: This method injects a mouse button press or release event at the given screen-space position, processed identically to a real hardware mouse event. Only UserInputType.MouseButton1, UserInputType.MouseButton2, and UserInputType.MouseButton3 are supported; passing any other value throws a runtime error. This method throws a runtime error if the specified position overlaps an interactive CoreGui element such as a button or an active overlay in the top bar, chat window, or escape menu. It also throws if the specified button is already in the requested state, for example pressing a button that is already pressed.

methods.name: SendMouseDelta
methods.documentation: This method injects a relative mouse movement event, representing how far the mouse moved rather than where it is on screen. This is intended for use while the player's cursor is locked, such as in first-person camera mode. This method throws a runtime error when the cursor is not locked. To move the cursor to an absolute screen position instead, use SendMousePosition(). *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe*

methods.name: SendMousePosition
methods.documentation: This method moves the virtual mouse cursor to the specified absolute screen-space position, processed identically to a real hardware mouse-move event. This method throws a runtime error when the specified position overlaps an interactive Roblox UI element (such as a button or active overlay in the top bar, chat window, or escape menu). To inject relative mouse movement while the cursor is locked, use SendMouseDelta() instead. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe*

methods.name: SendPointerAction
methods.documentation: This method injects a pointer action event at the given screen-space position. The pointerAction dictionary accepts the following keys: This method throws a runtime error if the specified position overlaps an interactive Roblox UI element (such as a button or active overlay in the top bar, chat window, or escape menu). If all values in pointerAction are zero, the call returns without injecting any event. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe*

methods.name: SendTextInput
methods.documentation: This method injects a text input event, routing the given string directly to the focused TextBox or the experience's text input handler as if the player typed it on a physical keyboard. This is useful for populating text fields without needing to simulate individual key presses. This method throws a runtime error if CoreGui has keyboard focus, which includes a TextBox inside CoreGui being focused, a CoreGui element selected for keyboard or gamepad navigation, or the in-game escape menu being open. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe*

classes.name: VirtualInputManager
classes.documentation: An internal service that offers no functionality to developers.

classes.name: VirtualUser
classes.documentation: VirtualUser is a service that allows you to record the inputs of a user, and then play it back to a limited extent.

classes.name: VisibilityCheckDispatcher
classes.documentation: Service that schedules and runs viewability checks for immersive ad instances in a place.

classes.name: Visit
classes.documentation: The Visit service is a backend service used by Roblox. Its functions are not accessible to developers in any form.

classes.name: VoiceChatService
classes.documentation: VoiceChatService is responsible for voice chat's high-level functionality.

properties.name: DefaultDistanceAttenuation
properties.documentation: This property controls the default distance attenuation curve assigned to any generated AudioEmitter instances in the default voice chat setup. This property only has an effect if EnableDefaultVoice and UseAudioApi are both enabled, since no AudioEmitters are otherwise generated.

properties.name: EnableDefaultVoice
properties.documentation: When enabled, each voice-eligible player can be heard as though they were speaking through their character. The implementation details of the voice setup depend on UseAudioApi. When UseAudioApi is Enabled, disabling this property disables the default setup, but AudioDeviceInput will still work. Conversely, when UseAudioApi is Disabled, disabling the default voice setup effectively disables voice chat altogether.

properties.name: EnableVoiceVolumeControls
properties.documentation: This RolloutState property controls whether Roblox's built-in voice chat volume controls are available to players, including a global voice chat volume slider and per-user volume adjustments. When set to Enabled, these controls are available to players. When set to Disabled, the built-in controls are hidden, though creators can still implement their own custom voice volume controls. Default follows the default for this feature. If UseAudioApi is disabled, this property has no effect and built-in controls will be hidden.

properties.name: UseAudioApi
properties.documentation: If Enabled, the voice chat setup is represented and controlled by AudioDeviceInput objects. More specifically: You can disable the default setup by setting VoiceChatService.EnableDefaultVoice to false. If Disabled, the voice chat setup is done through an internal-only system. Currently, setting this to Automatic has the same meaning as Disabled. However, in the future, Automatic will become Enabled, so that new experiences can achieve greater customization over voice.

methods.name: GetChatGroupsAsync
methods.documentation: Returns a sorted array of arrays of chat group IDs for the given players. Each chat group ID is a string that represents a communication-compatible group within the current universe. If two or more players share the same chat group ID, those players are eligible to voice chat with each other based on their age-check status, voice chat eligibility, and communication settings. This method is server-side only and intended for real-time use cases such as matchmaking and teleporting. Chat group IDs are unique to the current universe, may change over time, and should not be stored once the user has left the experience. While you can hold onto the data returned for the purposes of gameplay while th

methods.name: IsVoiceEnabledForUserIdAsync
methods.documentation: Returns whether or not the given user has voice enabled. On the client-side, this can only be used to check the voice status of the local player. On the server-side, this can only check the voice status for players in that server. This function can throw an error if the HTTP call fails. *Yields · Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Audio, Chat* Is Voice Enabled For User Id Async Demonstrates VoiceChatService:IsVoiceEnabledForUserIdAsync().

classes.name: VRService
classes.documentation: Service responsible for handling interactions between Roblox and Virtual Reality (VR).

properties.name: AutomaticScaling
properties.documentation: When set to VRScaling.World, Camera.HeadScale adjusts so that the scale of the world is seen from the avatar's perspective. A player with a small avatar will perceive the objects around them as larger than a player with a large avatar will.

properties.name: AvatarGestures
properties.documentation: When set to true, a VR player will be able to animate their hands and head using their controllers and headset. Set this to false for experiences where VR hand and head tracking conflicts with custom game mechanics, such as bespoke avatar rigs or weapon systems incompatible with IK-driven gestures. This property must be set on the server.

properties.name: ControllerModels
properties.documentation: Controls how the models representing the player's VR hand controllers are displayed (VRControllerModelMode). When set to Transparent, the controller models are shown with transparency; when set to Disabled, the controller models are not rendered. Defaults to Transparent.

properties.name: FadeOutViewOnCollision
properties.documentation: When true, a VR player's view fades to black when their head collides with an object. This property prevents players from being able to see through walls while in VR. The default value is true.

properties.name: GuiInputUserCFrame
properties.documentation: This property describes what UserCFrame is responsible for input in VR. For instance, if a VR headset is responsible, the value of this property will be UserCFrame.Head. To check if Roblox detects any VR devices, which would be responsible for input in VR, you can check the VREnabled property. VRService.GuiInputUserCFrame This example checks if Roblox detects a VR device. If a VR device is detected, this prints the name of the UserCFrame responsible for VR input. If not, this example prints "No VR device detected!".

properties.name: LaserPointer
properties.documentation: Controls the mode of the laser pointer that a VR player uses to point at and interact with the user interface (VRLaserPointerMode). Set it to Disabled to hide the laser pointer, Pointer to show a single pointer, or DualPointer to show a pointer for each hand. Defaults to Pointer.

properties.name: ThirdPersonFollowCamEnabled
properties.documentation: Read-only. Indicates whether the third-person follow camera is enabled for the VR user. Its value mirrors the user's VR comfort setting and updates automatically whenever the user changes that setting, firing a changed signal so that scripts can respond. It cannot be set from a script.

properties.name: VREnabled
properties.documentation: This property describes whether the user is using a virtual reality (VR) device. If a VR device is enabled, you can interact with its location and movement through methods such as UserInputService:GetUserCFrame(). You can also react to VR device movement using the UserInputService.UserCFrameChanged event. This property can only be used in a LocalScript. VR Head Tracking This example demonstrates how to implement a head tracking script that mirrors the movement of a virtual reality (VR) headset (the user's actual head) to their in-game character's head. The example first check if the user is using a VR device by checking the value of the VREnabled() property. This example only works if the us

methods.name: GetTouchpadMode
methods.documentation: This method returns the VRTouchpadMode indicating the mode of a specified VRTouchpad. The returned mode indicates how the user interacts with their touchpad to play the game. This can also be used alongside the several UserInputService VR methods and events. This method will only work when used in a LocalScript. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Input* VRService:GetTouchpadMode This example retrieves and prints the name of the user's current VRTouchpad.Left touchpad mode.

methods.name: GetUserCFrame
methods.documentation: This method returns a CFrame describing the position and orientation of a specified virtual reality (VR) device as an offset from a point in real world space. This method should be used when implementing VR compatibility into a game to obtain and track the movement of a connected VR device. By using the method, developers can implement features such as re-positioning the user's in-game character corresponding to the location of a connected VR device. This can be done by changing the _CFrame_ of the user's in-game character to match the _CFrame_ of the specified VR device using the UserCFrame enum and _CFrame_ value arguments passed by the event.

methods.name: GetUserCFrameEnabled
methods.documentation: This method returns true if the specified UserCFrame virtual reality device (VR) is available to be listened to. It can be used to determine whether a specified VR device, such as UserCFrame.Head, is connected to the user's game. This can also be used alongside the several UserInputService VR methods and events. This method will only work when used in a LocalScript. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Input* (true) or disabled (false). VRService:GetUserCFrameEnabled This example indicates whether the UserCFrame.Head VR device is enabled or disabled for the user. If the device is enabled, this prints "VR device is enabled!". If the device is disabled, this prints "VR devic

methods.name: RecenterUserHeadCFrame
methods.documentation: This method re-centers the CFrame of the user's head to the current location of the VR headset being worn by the user. It can be used to ensure that the user's in-game head is positioned according to the location of the user's VR headset. This behaves identically to UserInputService:RecenterUserHeadCFrame(). This method will only work when used in a LocalScript. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Input* VRService:RecenterUserHeadCFrame This example fires the function to recenter the CFrame of the user's head to the current location of the VR headset being worn by the user.

methods.name: RequestNavigation
methods.documentation: This method requests navigation to the specified CFrame using the specified UserCFrame as the origin for the visualizer parabola. It can be used to incorporate virtual reality (VR) into your game by providing a means to visualize a navigation path from the user's VR device to a destination. VRService has a similar event, NavigationRequested, used to detect such requests. This can also be used alongside the several UserInputService VR methods and events. This method will only work when used in a LocalScript. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Input* VRService:RequestNavigation

methods.name: SetTouchpadMode
methods.documentation: This method sets the mode of the specified VRTouchpad to the specified VRTouchpadMode. It can be used to change the user's virtual reality (VR) touchpad mode so that the user interacts with the game differently using the touchpad. This can also be used alongside the several UserInputService VR methods and events. This method will only work when used in a LocalScript. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Input* VRService:SetTouchpadMode This example sets the user's VRTouchpad.Left touchpad mode to TouchMode.Touch. This means that the left touchpad is treated as ButtonB.

events.name: NavigationRequested
events.documentation: This event fires when navigation is requested from VRService for a specified UserCFrame VR device. It fires with a CFrame coordinate and the specified UserCFrame indicating the device requesting the navigation. This event can be used alongside UserInputService service events and methods. Since this event fires locally, it can only be used in a LocalScript. *Security: None · Capabilities: Input* VRService.NavigationRequested This example prints the name of the UserCFrame VR device making the request, and the CFrame coordinates passed.

events.name: TouchpadModeChanged
events.documentation: This event fires if the VRTouchpadMode of a VRTouchpad is changed. You can use this event to track the states of VR touchpads connected via the user's client. This event can be used alongside UserInputService service events and methods. Since this event fires locally, it can only be used in a LocalScript. *Security: None · Capabilities: Input* VRService.TouchpadModeChanged This example fires when the state of a VRTouchpad changes. It prints the name of the Touchpad that changed, and the state that it changed to.

events.name: UserCFrameChanged
events.documentation: This event fires when a UserCFrame is changed, for instance when the user moves a connected VR device. It can be used alongside GetUserCFrame() to track the CFrame coordinates of a VR device, and when it changes/moves. It can also be used alongside UserInputService service events and methods. Since this event fires locally, it can only be used in a LocalScript. *Security: None · Capabilities: Input* VRService.UserCFrameChanged This event fires when the user moves a connected VR device. When the event fires, this prints the name of the VR device type that changed, and the updated CFrame coordinates.

events.name: UserCFrameEnabled
events.documentation: This event fires when a UserCFrame is enabled or disabled. It can be used alongside GetUserCFrameEnabled() to track whether a specified UserCFrame is enabled, and when its state changes. It can also be used alongside UserInputService service events and methods. Since this event fires locally, it can only be used in a LocalScript. *Security: None · Capabilities: Input* VRService.UserCFrameEnabled This example fires when a UserCFrame changes state, printing the name of the changed UserCFrame and whether it changed got enabled or disabled.

classes.name: WebStreamClient
classes.documentation: Maintains a streaming connection.

properties.name: ConnectionState
properties.documentation: The current WebStreamClientState of the client.

methods.name: Close
methods.documentation: Closes the client, aborting the ongoing request. If successful, fires the WebStreamClient.Closed event. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Network*

methods.name: Send
methods.documentation: Enqueues data to be transmitted to the server over the connection. Only works on clients created with WebStreamClientType.WebSocket. For other client types it does nothing. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Network*

events.name: Closed
events.documentation: Fires when the server closes the connection succesfully or the user calls WebStreamClient:Close() *Security: None · Capabilities: Network*

events.name: Error
events.documentation: Fires if an error is received while establishing the connection or during the connection lifetime. *Security: None · Capabilities: Network*

events.name: MessageReceived
events.documentation: Fires each time a message is received from the server. The format differs based on the WebStreamClientType. *Security: None · Capabilities: Network*

events.name: Opened
events.documentation: Fires when the a connection is successfully established between the client and server, allowing for events to begin streaming. Provides any response headers in raw format, which can be used for validation. *Security: None · Capabilities: Network*

classes.name: WedgePart
classes.documentation: A type of BasePart that has a wedge shape.

classes.name: Weld
classes.documentation: Holds two BaseParts together in a fixed relative position, regardless of whether they're touching.

classes.name: WeldConstraint
classes.documentation: Connects two BaseParts together such that their relative position and orientation remain the same.

properties.name: Active
properties.documentation: True if the WeldConstraint is currently active in the world. If the WeldConstraint or one of its parts is not in Workspace the weld will be inactive. Rigid joints like Weld, Snap, WeldConstraint, Motor, or Motor6D may also be disabled due to conflicts with other rigid joints, such as joints between the same two parts or indirect cycles in the weld graph. Joints disabled this way may be re-enabled later when another joint or part is added or removed. Duplicate WeldConstraints do not conflict because WeldConstraints derive their internal CFrames from the relative positions of their parts when they are enabled and all update when BasePart.Position or BasePart.Orientation is set on a part. The s

properties.name: Enabled
properties.documentation: The Enabled property of a WeldConstraint sets whether the constraint is active or not. When this property is set to true, if the constraint's WeldConstraint.Part0 and WeldConstraint.Part1 properties are set, then the constraint will ensure that its two connected parts will be locked together.

properties.name: Part0
properties.documentation: The Part0 and WeldConstraint.Part1 properties of a WeldConstraint set which two BasePart the weld connects. As soon as both properties are set and the weld is WeldConstraint.Enabled, the weld will lock the two parts together. If Part0 or Part1 are ever set to new parts, then the WeldConstraint will instantly link the new part. The old part will no longer be constrained. Part0 Demonstrates WeldConstraint.Part0.

properties.name: Part1
properties.documentation: The WeldConstraint.Part0 and Part1 properties of a WeldConstraint set which two BasePart the weld connects. As soon as both properties are set and the weld is WeldConstraint.Enabled, the weld will lock the two parts together. If Part0 or Part1 are ever set to new parts, then the WeldConstraint will instantly link the new part. The old part will no longer be constrained. Part1 Demonstrates WeldConstraint.Part1.

classes.name: Wire
classes.documentation: Connects one or more Instances to form a processing graph of their streams. At the moment, only audio streams are supported, but this may expand in the future.

properties.name: Connected
properties.documentation: Denotes whether the Wire is connected, meaning its SourceInstance, TargetInstance, SourceName, and TargetName properties are all assigned, the corresponding SourceName and TargetName pins exist on SourceInstance and TargetInstance respectively, and the connection does not result in a cyclic processing graph.

properties.name: SourceInstance
properties.documentation: The Instance producing a stream to be carried over the wire. At the moment, only audio streams are wirable.

properties.name: SourceName
properties.documentation: The name of the pin on SourceInstance that is producing a stream. At the moment, various audio instances only have an Output pin, but this may expand in the future. The default value of this property is Output so it is not yet necessary to change.

properties.name: TargetInstance
properties.documentation: The Instance intended to receive a stream from SourceInstance. Currently, only audio streams are wirable.

properties.name: TargetName
properties.documentation: The name of the pin on TargetInstance that is receiving a stream. At the moment, audio instances typically have an Input pin, but AudioCompressor has an additional Sidechain pin. This may expand in the future.

classes.name: WireframeHandleAdornment
classes.documentation: Renders a wireframe adornment consisting of one or more lines onto a BasePart (including Terrain) or into the Workspace.

properties.name: Scale
properties.documentation: This property specifies the XYZ scale of the wireframe adornment as a Vector3. For example, a scale of Vector3.new(1, 2, 1) will scale the adornment twice its normal size on the Y axis while keeping the X and Z axes unchanged.

properties.name: Thickness
properties.documentation: This property determines the thickness of the wireframe adornment's lines in pixels. Note that this visual thickness does not change relative to the adornment's distance from the viewer's camera.

methods.name: AddLine
methods.documentation: This method adds a line to the wireframe adornment from a starting point to an ending point, both defined as a Vector3 relative to the center of the Adornee. Note that you can make a multicolor wireframe by changing the adornment's Color3 property before new lines are drawn via AddLine(), as demonstrated in the following code sample. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Basic, UI* Multicolor Wireframe

methods.name: AddLines
methods.documentation: This method adds one or more lines of the current Color3 color to the wireframe adornment using an array. Each pair of Vector3 points in the array acts as a starting point and ending point for a line, relative to the center of the Adornee. Note that lines are rendered independently and their ending points are not connected to the starting point of any other line. To connect multiple line segments in a sequence from point to point, see AddPath(). *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Basic, UI* Wireframe Lines From Array

methods.name: AddPath
methods.documentation: This method adds multiple line segments of the current Color3 color to the wireframe adornment in a sequence from point to point. The path can be closed (ending point connected to starting point) by setting the loop parameter to true. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Basic, UI* Basic Path Wireframe

methods.name: AddText
methods.signature: WireframeHandleAdornment:AddText(point: Vector3, text: string, size?: int): ()
methods.documentation: Adds a text label to the wireframe adornment at a Vector3 point relative to the center of the Adornee. You can adjust the size of the text through the size parameter, and the label renders in the current Color3 color. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Basic, UI*

methods.name: Clear
methods.documentation: Instantly clears all lines and text in the wireframe adornment. *Security: None · Thread Safety: Unsafe · Capabilities: Basic, UI*

classes.name: Workspace

properties.name: Gravity
properties.documentation: Determines the acceleration due to gravity applied to falling BaseParts. This value is measured in studs per second squared and by default is set to 196.2 studs/second<sup>2</sup>. By changing this value, developers can simulate the effects of lower or higher gravity in game. Low Gravity Button This script creates a touch pad in the workspace that, when touched, will reduce the game's gravity. Activating the pad again will switch back to normal gravity.

properties.name: CurrentCamera
properties.documentation: The Camera object being used by the local player. When looking for a client's Camera object, use this property rather than looking for a child of Workspace named "Camera". When you set this property, all other Camera objects in the Workspace are destroyed, including the previous CurrentCamera. If you set this property to nil or to a camera that is not a descendant of the Workspace (or the CurrentCamera is otherwise destroyed), a new Camera will be created and assigned. Avoid these scenarios, as destroying the camera can have unintended consequences. For more information, see Script the camera.

properties.name: AirDensity
properties.documentation: The ground level (Y of 0) air density in RMU/stud³ units (see Roblox Units), used to calculate the aerodynamic force if Workspace.FluidForces is Experimental. The default corresponds to realistic sea level air density at standard temperature and pressure. Air density decays as the Y altitude increases, reaching 5% of its ground level value at 100,000 studs. Below Y of 0, the air density is fixed at the input value.

properties.name: AirTurbulenceIntensity
properties.documentation: Controls the intensity of turbulence by determining the magnitude of fluctuations in wind velocities. Ranges from 0 to 1, with a value of 0 disabling turbulence and a value of 1 providing the most intense turbulence. The values of AirTurbulenceIntensity roughly correspond to the following levels: The magnitude of the fluctuations at a fixed intensity scale linearly with the magnitude of the global wind, except in the case that the global wind is zero. When the global wind is zero, the magnitude of the fluctuations scale exponentially with AirTurbulenceIntensity, allowing low and high intensity turbulence to exist with wind velocities that still average out to zero.

properties.name: AllowThirdPartySales
properties.documentation: This Workspace property determines whether assets created by other uses can be sold in the game.

properties.name: AuthorityMode
properties.documentation: Sets the server authority mode. See AuthorityMode for options.

properties.name: AvatarUnificationMode
properties.documentation: When AvatarUnificationMode.Enabled, R15 avatars can join R6 experiences via the R6 to R15 adapter. R15 characters receive invisible adapter parts with R6-compatible names welded to their corresponding R15 parts, preserving R6-like scale and movement while enabling R15 features such as layered clothing and animatable heads. Only relevant when the experience's avatar type is set to R6.

properties.name: ClientAnimatorThrottling
properties.documentation: Specifies the ClientAnimatorThrottlingMode to use for the local client. When enabled, animations on remotely-simulated Model instances will begin to throttle. The throttler calculates throttling intensity using:

properties.name: DistributedGameTime
properties.documentation: The amount of time, in seconds, that the game has been running. Despite the title, this value is currently not 'Distributed' across the client and the server. Instead, on the server it represents how long the server has been running. On the client, it represents how long the client has been connected to the server. Developers should not rely on the above behavior, and it is possible this property will be synchronized across clients and the server in the future. Those looking for the time since the program started running should use the 'time' function instead. See below for a comparison between DistributedGameTime and its alternatives.

properties.name: EnableSLIMAvatars
properties.documentation: This RolloutState property controls whether a SLIM model is generated for avatar characters in the experience. When enabled and instance streaming is active, avatars render using SLIM in the same way that setting Model.LevelOfDetail to SLIM works for other models. When set to Enabled, avatars use SLIM rendering. When set to Disabled, avatars use the traditional rendering approach. Default follows the current engine-wide rollout state. This property cannot be set through developer-facing Luau and must be set in Studio through the Properties window, Command Bar, or a plugin.

properties.name: FallenPartsDestroyHeight
properties.documentation: This property determines the height at which the engine automatically removes falling BaseParts and their ancestor Models from Workspace by parenting them to nil. This is to prevent parts that have fallen off the map from continuing to fall forever. If a part removed due to this behavior is the last part in a Model, that model will also be removed. This applies to all model ancestors of the part. This property is clamped between -50,000 and 50,000 because BaseParts do not simulate or render properly at a great distance from the origin due to floating point inaccuracies. This property can be read by scripts, but can only be set by plugins, the command bar, or the properties window in Studio.

properties.name: FallHeightEnabled
properties.documentation: When false, the kill plane defined by Workspace.FallenPartsDestroyHeight is disabled and falling parts are not automatically removed. Defaults to true. This property can be read by scripts but can only be set by plugins, the command bar, or the properties window in Studio.

properties.name: FluidForces
properties.documentation: With this property enabled, the physics engine computes aerodynamic forces on BaseParts whose EnableFluidForces property is true. The default, Default, disables aerodynamic forces. Note that this property cannot be set through developer-facing Luau and instead must be toggled in Studio.

properties.name: GlobalWind
properties.documentation: This property specifies the direction and strength that wind blows through the experience, affecting terrain grass, dynamic clouds, and particles. See the Global Wind article for details.

properties.name: IKControlConstraintSupport
properties.documentation: Enables support for constraints for IKControls. The Default value is the same as Enabled. If disabled, IKControls ignore physics constraints. See IKControl for additional details.

properties.name: ImprovedAnimationConstraint
properties.documentation: When enabled, AnimationConstraints use separate strength and damping settings for linear and angular motion. Default follows the default for this feature.

properties.name: ImprovedPhysicsReplication
properties.documentation: When enabled, the experience uses the improved physics replication path. Default follows the default for this feature.

properties.name: InsertPoint
properties.documentation: Stores the world-space position used when inserting new objects into the workspace via the Studio IDE.

properties.name: LayeredClothingCacheOptimizations
properties.documentation: Controls whether the engine caches layered clothing rendering data to improve performance for experiences with many characters wearing layered clothing. Default follows the current engine-wide rollout state.

properties.name: LuauTypeCheckMode
properties.documentation: Controls the Luau type checking mode applied to scripts in the experience. See LuauTypeCheckMode for the available modes.

properties.name: MeshPartHeadsAndAccessories
properties.documentation: Sets whether character Heads and Accessories should be downloaded as MeshParts. The Default value is the same as Enabled. If this feature is enabled, built-in avatars will use MeshParts for the character's head and accessories.

properties.name: MeshStreamingAndImprovedLods
properties.documentation: This RolloutState property determines whether the experience uses the new mesh streaming and Wild Mesh Simplifier LOD system. When set to Enabled, mesh requests fetch the lowest quality LOD first and stream in higher detail over time. When set to Disabled, the legacy mesh loading behavior is used. Default follows the current engine-wide rollout state.

properties.name: ModelStreamingBehavior
properties.documentation: This ModelStreamingBehavior property controls how Models are replicated in experiences when instance streaming is enabled.

properties.name: NextGenerationReplication
properties.documentation: When true, enables an alternate replication system that alters and improves how properties are replicated under the hood; note that when true, you should not rely on the ordering of property replication and remote events.

properties.name: PathfindingUseImprovedSearch
properties.documentation: When Enabled, PathfindingService uses an improved pathfinding algorithm. Default follows the current engine-wide rollout state.

properties.name: PhysicsSteppingMethod
properties.documentation: Sets how the solver will advance the physics simulation forward in time. This option cannot be set through developer-facing Luau and must be set from the PhysicsSteppingMethod property of Workspace within Studio. See Adaptive Timestepping for details. Note that when assemblies of different simulation rates become connected via Constraints or collisions, the combined mechanism will default to the highest simulation rate for stability.

properties.name: PlayerCharacterDestroyBehavior
properties.documentation: When enabled, the engine automatically calls Destroy() on a player's old character when it is replaced (for example, on respawn) and on the Player object itself when the player leaves the server.

properties.name: PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem
properties.documentation: Controls whether the built-in player scripts are updated to use the Input Action System. When enabled, the player scripts live under StarterPlayer (controlled by StarterPlayer.CreateDefaultPlayerModule) and the server is able to process player inputs.

properties.name: PredictiveStreamingMode
properties.documentation: When enabled, the engine can prepare content for anticipated changes to a player's replication focus. This includes movement along likely paths, predicted spawn locations, and large changes in focus position. Default currently behaves like Disabled.

properties.name: PrimalPhysicsSolver
properties.documentation: The Primal Physics Solver is an experimental constraint solver that can improve accuracy in complex setup. Setting this property to Experimental enables it.

properties.name: RejectCharacterDeletions
properties.documentation: When enabled, the server ignores client requests to delete player character objects from the workspace, preventing exploits that attempt to abuse this replication path. Default is currently equivalent to Enabled.

properties.name: RenderingCacheOptimizations
properties.documentation: Controls whether the engine caches rendering state data to reduce redundant per-frame work. When enabled, the renderer can skip recomputing state for static objects, improving frame rates in scenes with many parts.

properties.name: ReplicateInstanceDestroySetting
properties.documentation: Determines the replication behavior when Instance:Destroy() is called on the server. When Enabled, the engine uses improved replication semantics for instance destruction.

properties.name: Retargeting
properties.documentation: Sets the animation retargeting mode. Retargeting adapts animations to character rigs of different proportions, allowing a single animation to play correctly on characters of varying sizes and shapes.

properties.name: SandboxedInstanceMode
properties.documentation: When set to Experimental, the engine enables sandboxed instance mode, which lets you use script capabilities.

properties.name: SignalBehavior
properties.documentation: This property determines whether event handlers will be resumed immediately when the event fires, or deferred and then resumed at a later resumption point. Resumption points currently include: For more information, see Deferred Events.

properties.name: StreamingEnabled
properties.documentation: This property determines whether in-experience content streaming is enabled for the place. This property is not scriptable and therefore must be set on the Workspace object in Studio.

properties.name: StreamingIntegrityMode
properties.documentation: If instance streaming is enabled, an experience may behave in unintended ways if a player's character moves into a region of the world that has not been streamed to their client. The streaming integrity feature offers a way to avoid those potentially problematic situations.

properties.name: StreamingMinRadius
properties.documentation: This property indicates the radius around the player's character or the current ReplicationFocus in which content will be streamed in at the highest priority. Defaults to 64 studs. Care should be taken when increasing the default minimum radius since doing so will require more memory and more server bandwidth at the expense of other components.

properties.name: StreamingTargetRadius
properties.documentation: This property controls the maximum distance away from the player's character or the current ReplicationFocus in which content will be streamed in. Defaults to 1024 studs. Note that the engine is allowed to retain previously loaded content beyond the target radius, memory permitting.

properties.name: StreamOutBehavior
properties.documentation: This property controls where content will be unloaded from the ReplicationFocus based on device memory conditions, or based on the streaming radius.

properties.name: Terrain
properties.documentation: This property is a reference to the Terrain object parented to the Workspace. !Terrain object within the Workspace hierarchy See Environmental Terrain for more information.

properties.name: TouchesUseCollisionGroups
properties.documentation: This property determines whether parts in different groups set to not collide will ignore collisions and touch events. By default, the value of this property is set to false. When this property is enabled, parts in different groups set to not collide will also ignore the CanTouch property, similar to how BasePart.CanCollide is ignored. For more information on the behavior of CanTouch, please visit its property page.

properties.name: UseFixedSimulation
properties.documentation: When true, enables RunService:BindToSimulation() which calls a function at a fixed frequency. Also updates physics stepping logic such that character controller updates and joint transforms are performed at a fixed frequency rather than once per frame, as well as makes the RobloxGlobals.time() function return the fixed stepped frame time.

properties.name: UseNewLuauTypeSolver
properties.documentation: This RolloutState property controls whether the new Luau type solver is used for type inference and type checking in scripts. The new type solver provides improved accuracy and performance for type analysis. Note that Workspace.LuauTypeCheckMode controls the mode (strict, nonstrict, etc.) while this property controls which solver implementation is active. Default follows the current engine-wide rollout state.

properties.name: FilteringEnabled
properties.documentation: Deprecated: This property is discontinued. This property is discontinued and no longer takes effect.

properties.name: InterpolationThrottling
properties.documentation: Deprecated: This property should not be used for new work. This property has Physics read security and Plugin write security. It is hidden in the Studio Properties window. Do not use it for new work.
